## P04 (part 1): deterministic responsibility checks

- `ResponsibilityChecks` (`projects/checks.ts`): `generate(by, projectId)` records one `responsibility-check` for each active, scheduled responsibility whose next check is due, identified by responsibility and slot (so a repeat, a restart or a second instance records nothing new). After downtime one catch-up check is owed with the gap named (`missedChecks`, start, end), not one per slot. A check inside a maintenance window is owed and says so. `pending(by, projectId)` lists those not yet finished by a `check` observation recorded after the slot. Owner, service or `responsibility.write` may generate; reading follows `responsibility.read`. It records only that a check is owed: no task, model or action.
- **Not here (P04b):** a loop that runs `generate` on the controller's clock; turning a due check into a bounded task or an observation; incident grouping with retries and escalation; observed state kept apart from intended state ("no recent observation" is never healthy); maintenance leases; API operations and the status view; the event-driven checks. Provisional defaults still to be chosen by the owner: who pays for check tasks, grouping window, retry and escalation counts, and whether actions are held in a maintenance window (assumed yes).

## P04 (part 2): incidents and observed state

- `IncidentService` (`projects/incidents.ts`): `report` groups alerts (`attention`/`failed`) with the same signature on one responsibility into one open incident (count, first and last time, worst outcome); a resolved signature that alerts again opens a new incident. `resolve` needs evidence. `escalate(by, projectId)` marks each open incident escalated once (to the responsibility's `escalation.to`) when `escalation.afterMinutes` has passed since it opened; repeats and other instances record nothing new; resolved ones never. `observed` tells what the checks found apart from the desired condition: `unknown` with no check or one older than twice the period, never healthy by default; open incidents show as attention or failed. Authority is the same as for adding history (owner, the responsible agent, `responsibility.write`).
- **Not here (P04c):** the bounded retry count before escalation (only the time rule exists), a loop that runs `generate` and `escalate` on the clock, turning an escalation into an owner notice, turning a due check into a bounded task, API operations and the status view, maintenance leases, event-driven checks, and the coverage-gap record from an outage of the event source.

## P04 (part 3): wired into the running controller

- A dispatcher loop (`responsibilities.checks`) runs `ResponsibilityChecks.generate` and `IncidentService.escalate` for every project on each tick, as the tick's principal.
- State API: `responsibility.checks` (due checks not yet finished), `responsibility.incidents`, `responsibility.observed`, and the commands `incident.report` and `incident.resolve`.
- Remaining in P04 (P04c): the bounded retry count, turning a due check into a bounded task and an escalation into an owner notice, maintenance leases, event-driven checks, coverage gap from an event-source outage, and the chat/status view.

## H10 (part 1): child tasks with allowances, and swarm cancellation

- `SwarmService` (`swarm/`): `spawn` makes a child task, writes its contract from the parent's outcome and acceptance criteria, delegates part of the parent's budget to it (R05, so it can spend only that), and records a `swarm-link` (child -> parent). It refuses a parent that has nothing to give (budget `delegate` refuses), a task already at the depth limit (3) or with 4 live children (the H03 defaults, overridable), and cancels a child it made before a refusal so no task is left without an allowance. Authority is the budget's: the owner or the holder of the parent's node with `budget.manage`. `cancel` stops every descendant deepest first (Stop, not Suspend), takes back what each did not use (`reclaim`), cancels the task, and reports `settled` and `pending`; repeating it is safe. State API: `swarm.spawn`, `swarm.cancel`.
- **Provisional decisions (to put to the owner at the end of the batch):** who may spawn (budget holders and the owner for now, not any agent with `task.create`), cancel means Stop (not Suspend) and unused allowance returns automatically, depth 3 and 4 children stay the defaults, and "bounded coordination" (a cap on messages a parent receives from children) is not defined by the card and not built.
- **Not here (H10b):** the dispatcher does not yet pass the parent to admission, so depth/children limits at admission still do not fire for real spawns (the swarm service enforces them itself); a child with no budget node is not blocked from starting; stop/review/inquiry requests are not yet made through admission's control class; per-project or per-tree caps and host quotas beyond the existing `perHost`/`productive`; a chat command.

## Batch 14 review fixes (L06, P04, H10)

- **H10.** `spawn` and `cancel` first check who may (the owner, or the holder of the parent's budget with `budget.manage` and, for `spawn`, `task.create` in the project; new read `BudgetService.canManage`), before making any task or reporting any limit, so a foreign task answers `forbidden` and nothing is made. A retry of a spawn that was refused and cancelled its child, with the same command ID, is refused ("ask again with a new command ID") instead of giving that cancelled task an allowance. `cancel` takes back a child's unused allowance before cancelling it; a caller who cannot reclaim leaves the child pending, so a later call by someone who can still finds it.
- **P04.** An escalated incident whose `escalatedTo` is `owner` becomes a `maintenance` notice (command `inc-esc-<id>`); one project failing no longer skips the others in a tick. The scans of checks and incidents allow 50,000 records.
- **Known, not fixed:** the live-children limit is a check then act, so two simultaneous spawns could pass the 4-child limit (the depth, node and budget limits hold); check and incident records are never pruned and are read by scanning all (an index per project and a retention rule belong to K06/P04c); escalation to an agent (not `owner`) sends no notice; the L06 tracked-remote-job exception is decided from the job's own fields (`kind`, `background`, `resumability`), which the admitting agent sets, so an agent could tag a job to be listed as tracked rather than waited for (it is shown to the owner as an exception, and Force Stop still works) — a permission for the tag belongs with L01's background permission.
- **Batch 14, second pass.** An escalation is told once it has been told: `IncidentService.untold` lists escalated incidents with no `notifiedAt` and `markNotified` records the notice, so a notice that could not be sent (for example the owner has too many open items) is offered again next tick, and an escalation recorded before an error is not lost. `swarm.cancel` checks that the caller holds the child's parent budget before stopping anything, so a child is never left stopped but not cancelled. Known: an escalation to an agent (not `owner`) still sends no notice.

## T02 (part 1): set aside and roll back catalog versions

- `CatalogService.deprecate` (owner only) sets a version aside: it is no longer chosen when a caller names no version, but a task that names it still resolves and runs it (silent resume does not break) and it stays readable. `rollback(name, toVersion)` sets aside every published, unrevoked version above the target (the target comes back into use if it had been set aside; a revoked target is refused). Nothing is deleted or rewritten; a revoked version stays refused. Non-maintainer publication was already refused (only the registrant's own accepted work, the owner for shared and system names).
- **Not here (T02b):** the state API and chat for the catalog (it has no operations at all yet), promotion of a personal artifact to the shared layer, the in-flight policy on revocation (finish, cancel or pause: an owner decision, provisional default is to refuse new runs and let a running one finish), paused-task migration to a newer version, the retention of stale referenced artifacts (K06), and a personal fork of a revoked tool gaining no authority (new registrations are checked against grants already; no fork operation exists).

## U06b: recovery chat controls for routes and providers

- The typed orders `/nimblenewt.routing-disable`, `-drain`, `-cutover` and `-reenable` are recovery orders (the same class as pause and stop): they run as typed, need no assistant, and report Received, Accepted and Effected (new work no longer reaches the target; how many running attempts a cutover cancelled; or that the target may be used again). The records, owner-only checks and restart behaviour are R04b's.
- Short forms `/exclude`, `/restore` and `/cutover <model|endpoint|account|provider|service> <name> [reason]` (`chat/shorthand.ts`) are never run: the chat answers with the exact typed line they stand for ("it has not run; send the line as it is") and the owner sends that line. An incomplete short form is told what is missing. `/drain` has no short form because it needs a duration the owner must choose.
- Provisional: short forms are shown rather than confirmed with a yes/no because the chat has no place to hold a pending typed line; the owner can say otherwise.

## X09 (part 1): external release-test job protocol

- `release/release.ts` (`ReleaseService`, state API `release.*`). The owner submits an immutable **candidate** (source commit, artifact hashes, dependency-lock hashes, suite revision, platform matrix); its ID is a digest of the ordered manifest, so the same manifest is the same candidate. Each platform is tested by **attempts**: the owner authorizes a host for destructive release tests on one platform (`release.host`; a production machine is not authorized by that) and issues an attempt to that host and a named worker; the job payload is a pure function of candidate, platform, attempt and limits.
- A **result** (`release.report`) is taken only from the worker the attempt was issued to (anyone else reads like a missing attempt; the owner may not report), only for an open attempt, and only if source commit, suite revision, artifact hashes and platform equal the candidate's; otherwise it is refused and counts for nothing. A pass needs passing tests and none failing. Summaries are redacted. A worker holds only the new action `release.report`; approval is owner-only and refused unless every platform's latest attempt passed (a platform with no attempt blocks it).
- A lost worker is `release.interrupt` (owner), never a pass; a retry is a new attempt with a new ID and the earlier attempts and their evidence stay. A platform that passed cannot be re-issued.
- No model is involved anywhere in submitting, issuing, reporting or gating.
- **Not here (X09b):** delivering the payload to a remote worker over the worker transport and collecting logs and artifact hashes from it (H12a), who notices a lost worker and interrupts the attempt (the owner does it by hand for now), the outer test supervisor for reboot and partition tests with an external effect sink (X10), and a chat wording for these orders.
- Provisional: log and artifact bytes are not stored, only the log digest and the artifact hashes the worker reports; a worker reports once per attempt.

## L03g (part 2): drafts and responsibilities in the hand-off package

- `controllerHandoffSources` takes three optional sources. **Drafts:** the sender's shared draft desk records on this task (status `draft`, visibility `shared`; private scratch, other tasks' drafts and accepted notes are left out), read as the sender, because a recipient could not otherwise read another agent's draft; each is `id "title": first 300 characters`. **Responsibilities** (a new fixed section name, `responsibilities`): the active responsibilities in the task's project that the sender answers for, with a line saying they stay with the sender until reassigned. **Locks:** a hook for what the sender holds locked or leased; no service keeps such holds yet (the integrator lease is P10, workspace holds H12m), so none is wired and the section stays unset rather than claiming "no locks".
- A failing source leaves its section missing; it never fails the package. The recipient's eligibility checks (L03d) are unchanged. Responsibilities are not transferred by a hand-off; moving them is a separate, deliberate reassignment (owner decision to confirm).
- **Remainder (L03h):** the `locks` source once something holds locks, and offering to reassign the sender's responsibilities with the task.

## V02b (part 1): an undecided stall concern is told to the owner

- `StallService.escalateUndecided` marks a suspected concern that has waited `escalateAfterMs` (provisional 30 minutes) without a decision as escalated and returns the escalated concerns whose notice is not recorded as sent; `markEscalationNotified` records it. The concern stays routed to its supervisor (who can still decide) and later scans keep the marks. The recovery loop (`recovery.stall-scan`) sends a `maintenance` notice about the task after each scan and offers it again next tick if sending failed. Needs the same right as the scan.
- **Not here (V02b2):** persisting an intervention and queued input before a stuck request is cancelled (needs the action ladder), recording the context carried on a fallback switch, loop recovery that keeps history and effects, assessing a supervisor's own task, and keeping the stall evidence across a new generation.

## H12b (part 1): the live worker is confined, and dies with its controller

- `packages/integration/src/h12b-confinement.test.ts` (with `h12b-confinement-support.ts` and a crash fixture `h12b-confinement-child.ts`) looks at the real worker process in the real bubblewrap sandbox, from the host's `/proc`: the worker's namespace has only the loopback device; the git directory is not mounted anywhere in it; the protected `.git` is mounted read-only (with a positive control that it is mounted); and a recipe with `processes: 64, memoryMb: 768` is enforced in full by a systemd scope whose `pids.max` and `memory.max` are exactly those numbers. A second test starts the controller side as a child process, kills it with SIGKILL and shows no process of the worker is left (with a positive control that it was running).

## H12f (part 1): a message told mid-turn

- Audit (2026-10-30): the controller side of H12f is built and composed (`controllerGuards` in `api/dispatch-compose.ts`: context admit/resume, pause observation, message boundaries); what was unproven was the real worker process taking a message while a turn runs. A test now holds a turn at the bridge wait, tells a message, and shows it is answered while the turn is still waiting, the turn completes, and the model sees the message on its next call.
- **Fix:** the worker process answered `tell.ok` only when the turn it landed in ended, so the host's per-beat delivery (`observeAndDeliver`) sat on that answer and could not report `paused` or deliver anything else for the rest of the turn. It now answers when the update is placed; a later failure of the placed update is a fault with the same ID (**wrong: see the review fixes below; it is not reported**).
- **Open for H12f (not claimed):** `compact` is missing on the host runtime and channel, so an over-budget first call always fails the attempt instead of compacting once; `systemPromptChars` is never sent in `ready` (an 8000-character fallback is used); a recipe change restarts without re-running the resume/admission checks; `confirmUsage` has no caller; `inFlight` counts only tool calls, not a streaming model call, so `paused` can be reported while a provider call is still open (owner/Opus question); pause behaviour is not exercised against the real process.

## H12f (part 2): the first call can be compacted once

- The worker channel has a `compact` request and a `compact.ok` answer (contracts, parsed and round-trip tested). The worker process compacts its stored conversation (`adapter.root().compact()`) and answers with the new size estimate, or a fault with the same ID; the host `WorkerProcess.compact()` asks and the host runtime offers `compact` (optional on `HostRuntime`), which is what `LocalWorker` already calls when `guards.context.admit` refuses the first call (round 1), so the request can be made. **Correction (Opus review, 2026-10-30): this does not yet make an over-budget first call pass.** The first-call description (`FirstCall` in `context/dispatch.ts`) has no term for the stored conversation, so compacting changes none of its inputs; and a refusal in round 1 opens a `context_overflow` blocker that makes round 2 refuse too. Making compaction work needs the stored size in the admission and a way past the blocker for a compacted call; it is not done and H12f stays open. Tested in the process (a turn, then compact, then the process answers a checkpoint). Not tested against a real model's summary: the offline model scripts the summary.
- Still open for H12f: `systemPromptChars` in `ready`, re-checking on a recipe change, a caller for `confirmUsage`, the streaming-call question for `paused`, pause against the real process.

## Review fixes for H12d, H12b and H12f (Opus, 2026-10-30)

- **H12d:** recovery did not lift a freeze left by a `release` request (the freeze-tag pattern in `workspace-ops.ts` listed integration, refresh and quarantine only); a controller crash during a release would leave the attempt frozen. Fixed, with a test that fails without the fix.
- **H12f:** the late failure of a placed `tell` was sent as a fault with no ID, which the host reads as "the process cannot go on" and fails the running turn. It is no longer sent (the host has no one waiting on it after `tell.ok`); the earlier note claiming a fault with the same ID was wrong. Compaction is corrected above.
- **H12b:** the git-directory-not-mounted check could never fail (`mountinfo` writes a space as `\040` and the temp directory name has spaces); it now decodes the escapes. The parent-death test now records the numbers of the worker's own processes (the descendants of the ones that name the host directory) before the kill and checks those are gone, not only the processes that name the host directory (which are only bwrap).
- Not changed: the cgroup check is skipped when the scope's files cannot be read, so "enforced in full" is only as strong as that read; `NIMBLENEWT_REQUIRE_LIMITS=1` makes a skip a failure.
- **Second pass (Opus):** decoding the whole mountinfo text before splitting broke the read-only `.git` check (a decoded space splits a field), so each field is decoded after the split; and a mount's root is relative to its own filesystem, so on a machine whose `/tmp` is its own filesystem the git-directory check named a path that could not appear; it now matches the last two parts of the path.

## L06b (part 1): a pause lifted on the owner's recorded time

- `PauseService.setResumeCondition(owner, { scope, at })`: the owner records, ahead of time, a UTC time after which the pause on that scope is lifted. Owner only; the scope must be paused now; setting it again replaces it. It is stored on the gate (`resumeAt`) and belongs to that pause: a resume or a new pause builds a new gate body and drops it.
- `PauseService.liftDue(by)` (dispatcher principal: owner, host or service): lifts the gates whose time has come, only that scope, as a normal `resume` request whose reason names the condition and who set it; the command ID is derived from the pause's request ID, so a repeat tick or a restart lifts nothing twice, and a gate that someone resumed or paused again in the meantime is skipped. A gate with no condition is never touched. Wired as the dispatcher loop `lifecycle.resume-conditions` and the state API operation `lifecycle.resume-condition` (so the chat assistant can record it for the owner).
- Replaces the "no automatic return" rule only for a pause that has a recorded condition; time alone still lifts nothing.
- **Provisional (owner to confirm):** the only condition kind is "not before this time"; other kinds (a meeting ended, an event, a person's answer) are not built. A re-pause by anyone drops the condition (the safer reading of "a condition belongs to the pause it was set for").
- **K06 audit finding:** nothing can delete stored thinking yet: the Pi conversation is append-only through the adapter and `ThinkingService` has a read-only `ThinkingSource` which is not wired in `startController`; K06's deletion needs adapter support first (rewriting or dropping thinking blocks in stored entries), so it is not a first-slice card.

## U11b (part 2): escalation to Urgent by age

- `NotificationService.runDue` (the scheduler tick, outside quiet hours) now raises an item that waits on the owner (kinds blocker, review-request, owner-question) to Urgent once it has been unanswered for the owner's threshold (`escalateAfterHours`, default 24, 1 to 720, set with `configure`). The item is marked `urgent`, `immediate` and `escalatedAt`, and told once as `URGENT, unanswered for N hours: ...` (the controller-built label only goes outside). Only this tick raises it (a producer still cannot); a repeat of the tick, a restart or a later tick does not tell it again; an answered item, a maintenance or presence item is left alone; inside quiet hours it waits until they end.
- Not done (U11b stays open, no flip): a level field on every item and a Notice that never pushes; the other Urgent triggers that belong to other cards (backup overdue K01, host down H01/H09, integrity A08, a watchdog, "the agent has nothing else to do"); the owner-facing way to set `escalateAfterHours` (`configure` is not a state API operation yet).

## Review fixes for L06b and U11b (Opus, 2026-10-30)

- **L06b:** a Stop, a Suspend (and so a hand-off) that reused an owner-paused gate kept its recorded time, which would have undone it later. `StopService.request/force` now drop the condition (`PauseService.dropResumeCondition`), and `liftDue` skips a gate whose observed state is preparing-to-suspend, suspended, stopping, stopped or recovery-required. The lift checks the pause it read: it applies only if the gate still has the same pause request, the same time and the time is due, so a gate resumed and paused again (or given a later time) between the list and the lift is skipped. A time must carry its zone (`Z` or an offset). One gate that cannot be lifted no longer stops the others (the first failure is raised after the scan).
- **U11b:** the record an item points at is checked again before it is raised: a blocker resolved, a review decided or a question settled in its own flow is not raised as Urgent. A failure to raise one item no longer skips the release of urgent reviews and the digests.
- Not changed: `liftDue` still scans every gate every tick (gates are never deleted; an index of gates with a condition is a later change, K06-like growth); the item for a record settled elsewhere is still never closed (no notification-side settle path exists).
- **Second pass (Opus):** the settled-record test was vacuous (the item was too young to reach the check); it now reports the item with the first one, and was shown to fail with the check removed. A pause that a Stop, Suspend or hand-off took over is marked `takenOver` on the gate (ends with the pause): no time can be recorded for it afterwards and `liftDue` skips it, so the guard no longer depends on the observed state alone. Not tested separately: the `liftDue` observed-state skip, the re-pause race guard, the deferred per-gate failure and the drop in `force()`; the order of the drop and the Stop request (a refused Stop request leaves the drop done, which is harmless because the pause is taken over by the earlier stop that caused the refusal).

## P04c (part 1): the bounded retry count before escalation

- A responsibility's `escalation` may carry `afterAlerts` (2 to 1000) besides `afterMinutes`: `IncidentService.escalate` escalates an open incident once its count of alerts (same signature) reaches it, or once the time has passed; either rule is enough. A rule the owner did not set applies to nothing, so there is no default retry count and nothing changes for existing responsibilities. Tested: two alerts do not escalate, the third does at once and only once, a duty with only the time rule is not escalated by count, a value of 1 is refused.
- Provisional: the owner has not chosen a default count; it is opt-in per responsibility until they do. Still open in P04c: turning a due check into a bounded task, maintenance leases, event-driven checks, the coverage gap from an event-source outage, the chat/status view.

## L06b: two review gaps covered by tests

- Force Stop drops a recorded time and marks the pause taken over; a pause whose runtime reports it `stopped` is not lifted by an old time. (The re-pause race guard and the deferred per-gate failure are covered in the next section.)

## M02e (part 1): a meeting can decide a budget raise or a grant

- **Owner decision 2026-10-30** (asked as "may the controller carry out an agreed widening?"): it depends on the setting, like most things. A specific permission, changeable through chat, decides; with none set, the installation profile decides (strict, derived or autonomous). This is what the existing `widening` hook in `startController` already does through `PolicyService.classMode` (an explicit cell wins; the profile otherwise; rights widen only where the owner set the cell by hand, because the table keeps access-change a decision for the owner in every profile). Nothing new was needed in the policy engine.
- New appliers registered with the meeting records: `budget.raise` (`budgetRaiseApplier`, widens `spend`, the carrying agent must hold `budget.manage`) and `grant.add` (`grantApplier`, widens `access-change`, the carrying agent must hold `principal.manage`). Each is carried out as the controller's own service identity through `BudgetService.raiseAgreed` / `GrantService.grantAgreed`, which are closed to everyone but a service or the owner. Both take exactly what the decision named: a raise names a task and positive amounts and nothing else; a grant names a project (not all projects), one agent, one action and an end time, is a direct grant (never standing), and keeps the decision and who allowed it (`owner:agreed` or `policy:<class>`) in its basis (a raise keeps them in the command's detail). A repeat after a crash does it once.
- `MeetingRecordService` passes `agreedBy` to `ChangeApplier.apply` (`owner:agreed` when the owner agreed, else `policy:<class>`).
- Tested at three levels: the services (`raiseAgreed`, `grantAgreed`: exact effect, repeat, refused callers and shapes), the appliers (shape checks, what reaches the service), and the existing widening flow of the record service (waits for the owner unless the policy lets the class through, refuses if the policy tightened).
- **Not done (M02e stays open):** an ownership-change applier; the decision log and the steward agent; the narrator; chat commands; the `shareable` check (still none passed in `start.ts`); a test of the full meeting vote → policy leave → real budget/grant effect through `startController`; chat wording that says an access-change cell set by hand also lets a meeting decision through (today the chat text says changing access "always stays your decision", which is true for agents' tool use and not for this path).

## C09i follow-up: one step's explanations without reading the task's all

- The task's explanation index now also keeps `bySeq` (step number to the ids of its contemporaneous explanations), so `explanationsFor(seq)` (and so `explainLater` and the `explanations` view with a step) reads only that step's records, not up to 2000. Results are unchanged.
- An index made before this keeps no `bySeq` and is read in full as before (and stays that way, since a partial lookup would miss the older entries). The caps (2000 / 200) are unchanged; they are a deliberate bound on the index size.
- Test: 60 explanations on one step and one on another; both are reachable, and the call for the single one reads under 12 records (counted by wrapping `CommandRunner.get`). Not done: the listing without a step (`explanations(taskId)`) still reads every entry.
## P04c follow-up: an incident escalated to an agent reaches that agent

- Before: `notify` in `api/start.ts` sent a notice only when `escalatedTo === "owner"`; for an agent id it did nothing, and the loop then marked the incident notified, so the escalation was silently lost.
- Channel chosen: `AgentMessageService.noticeFromController` (the controller-to-agent inbox notice the budget-holder and meeting notices already use), not a new channel. Text is built by the controller (signature, count, ids; the signature is already limited and redacted at recording). Filed once per incident through `commandId: inc-esc-<id>`; the existing `notifiedAt` marker still means "told".
- An incident has no task, and a notice must be about a task the recipient can read, so it is anchored to a task the agent holds now in the incident's project (`assignedTaskIn`). With none, the send fails (`unavailable`), the incident stays untold and is offered again next tick. Open: an agent with no task never gets it (a project-level notice anchor would fix that).
- `responsibilityLoops` now tries every untold incident of a project; one failed send no longer holds back the rest (first error raised at the end).

Two operations added, wired through `Context`, `StateApi` deps and `start.ts` (the same `notifications` service the rest of the controller uses): the query `notifications.settings` (owner only; the settings with their revision) and the command `notifications.configure` (owner only; `channel`, `channelName`, `digestTimes`, `quietHours`, `escalateAfterHours`, `expectedRevision`; passes through with the commandId, so the service's validation, `stale_revision` and replay apply unchanged). A task credential is refused for both.

## H10 follow-up: concurrent spawns and the live-children limit

- `SwarmService.spawn` counted live children and then created the child, so spawns sent at the same moment for one parent could all pass the check (5 of 5 got through a limit of 3 in the new test).
- Now each child claims a place on a per-parent `swarm-gate` record (`{ children: [...] }`) after it is made: the live count (linked plus claimed, minus finished) and the claim commit as one `create`/`update` with `expectedRevision`; a spawn that loses the race re-counts and retries (up to 50 times). A refused one cancels its child as before. Finished claims are dropped when the record is next written.
- Test: `spawns sent at the same moment cannot take a parent over its live-children limit` in `packages/controller/src/swarm/swarm.test.ts` (fails before the fix, passes after). The swarm suite only runs on SQLite; the PostgreSQL path was not exercised (no server here).
## L06b: the re-pause race and the per-gate failure of `liftDue` are tested

- New test hook `beforeLift(scope)` (runs after `liftDue` decided a gate is due, before it lifts it). Tested: a gate resumed by hand and paused again, or given a later time, between the read and the lift is not lifted; a gate whose lift throws a non-`invalid_command` error does not stop the others, and the first failure is thrown after the scan.
- `liftDue` does not return the lifted scopes when it throws; it takes an optional `onLifted(scope)` callback, called as each is lifted, for a caller that needs them.

## Backup race test: replacement already made when the second waiter resumes

- The fix in `BackupService.backUpFor` (`current !== known` check) stops a second repeat of one command ID, waiting on a removed backup, from starting another replacement after the first waiter's replacement was made and finished. The old test only covered the case where the replacement still ran, which the "one backup at a time" guard in `backUpNow` hid.
- Test: `two repeats waiting on a removed backup start exactly one replacement...` in `packages/controller/src/backup/backup.test.ts`. A subclass makes `backUpNow` finish at once without sharing a running backup, so the finished-first interleaving is forced and no timing is involved. With the check removed from the compiled file the test fails (2 starts, expected 1); restored, the backup suite passes (12/12).

## U11b follow-up: items settled elsewhere are closed

- `NotificationService.runDue` now first runs `#closeSettled`: a blocker, review-request or owner-question item whose record is no longer waiting on the owner (blocker resolved, review decided, inquiry answered or gone) gets state `settled` with `settledAt`, and leaves the inbox index, so no later digest or escalation carries it. It runs in quiet hours too (nothing is told).
- `settled` is a new `ItemBody.state`. It is treated like `answered` for re-reports (a new occurrence opens), escalation, digest completion; `answerItem` on a settled item is refused (`invalid_command`).

## U11b follow-up: the Needs-you view names the sources it cut

- `StatusService.needsYou` now also returns `truncated`: the sources that had more than the 50 read (`questions` when `ownerQuestions` gives a `next`, `approvals` when `ownerPending` has a 51st, `blockers` when a 51st open owner blocker is found or the 20-page scan ends). Under the cap it is `[]`. The closing line names them ("more questions, blockers than could be looked at") in place of the old blockers-only note, which also fired wrongly when there were exactly 50. `count`, ranking and the lines are otherwise unchanged. `ownerPending` is now asked for 51 and cut to 50.

### L06b/L02: the stop `seen` map survives a restart

- **Where and what.** The `seen` map is in `dispatchStopPorts` (`lifecycle/dispatch-ports.ts`), not `stop.ts`: the attempts seen for a scope, so a process of one that ended during preparation is still asked about when the stop ends. Earlier notes said it was "lost on restart". Checked: it was really lost (after a restart the dispatcher's live list no longer holds an attempt that ended, and the stop intent kept only inventory items, not attempt IDs), so a process of such an attempt would be missed by the terminate look and the stop could be reported clean.
- **Fix.** The stop intent body has `attempts` (up to 100 IDs). `StopPorts` gains optional `attempts(scope)` and `remember(scope, ids)`: after each cleanup the service records the attempts the runtime saw; at every advance it gives the recorded ones back to the runtime, which merges them into `seen`. No new storage; the existing intent record carries it. The map is still cleared when the stop ends or is released.
- **Tested.** `stop.test.ts` (both backends): a crash in terminate, a new service over the same storage, the sweep gives the runtime back both attempts. `dispatch-ports.test.ts`: a fresh ports object given the recorded attempts asks about them and reports the still-running process as unresolved.

## H12f: `confirmUsage` caller audit (2026-10-30)

- The "`confirmUsage` has no caller" gap in the H12f notes is stale. C07b already wired it: `ModelRelay.forAttempt({ onFirstUsage })` reads the provider's reported input tokens from the first reply; `confirmFirstCall` in `api/dispatch-compose.ts` passes them to `guards.context.confirm`, which calls `ContextEnforcementService.confirmUsage` against the round of the latest admitted first call (`controllerGuards` in `dispatch/runtime-guards.ts`). Covered by `relay.test.ts`, `runtime-guards.test.ts` and `start-dispatch.test.ts`.
- The count is deliberately taken at the controller's relay, not from the worker process: the worker channel carries no usage message, and the relay sees the raw provider reply. No new channel message is needed.
- What is still open: no production code builds a worker host through `local.build` (the host composer, H12k), so the live path is exercised only by those tests; no test runs the fake-model worker path through to a stored `confirmUsage` record end to end.
### H10 follow-up: swarm limit claims tested for leaks and on every backend

- Reviewed the `swarm-gate` claim in `swarm.ts`: each write keeps only claimed children that are not final plus the new one, so a cancelled or finished child's claim is dropped on the next write; a refusal writes nothing. No leak found, no source change.
- `swarm.test.ts` now runs on every backend in `backends` (reference store, SQLite, SQLite worker, PostgreSQL), building the services directly: the concurrent-spawn test (also asserts the claim list holds exactly the linked children), a failed spawn whose claim is dropped by the next write, a crash after the claim (allowance step and clean-up both fail) that holds a place only until the orphan is cancelled, and repeated spawn/finish cycles with the stored claim list asserted within the limit. The old startController/SQLite test stays.
- Known by design: a crashed, never-linked child keeps its place until something finishes or cancels it.
## L06b follow-up: the tick reads an index of timed gates

`PauseService.liftDue` used to list every `pause-gate` on every tick. `setResumeCondition` now writes, in the same operation, a small `pause-timed` entry per scope (id = the gate id; body `{ scope, at, active }`). The tick lists only that index and reads a gate only when its entry is active and due, so gates with no recorded time are never read. The gate stays the truth: before lifting, the tick checks the gate still holds that very time and pause. An entry whose gate was resumed, taken over or given another time is retired (inactive) or moved to the gate's new time the first time it comes due; a lost race leaves it for the next tick. Entries are never deleted (the store has no delete), so the index grows with the number of scopes ever timed, not with all gates. Gates stopped or suspended after being timed stay active in the index and are skipped when due. Tests: `pause-lift-scan.test.ts` (counts gate reads and lists through a storage proxy).

## L06b follow-up: the `pause-timed` index follows its gate

Depends on branch `wip/nn-sa-lift1793371678` (the index itself). An entry is now made inactive in the same operation that ends its condition: `resume` (an extra `update` Change on the entry inside the resume command) and `dropResumeCondition` (takeover). Re-pausing needs no change, since a pause is only possible after a resume, which already retired the entry. `liftDue` also retires (rather than skips) an entry whose gate is observed stopping, stopped, suspended, preparing-to-suspend or recovery-required, so such a gate is read once when its time comes and never again. Stop/Suspend commands themselves are not changed; the tick (or an earlier dropResumeCondition by the hand-off) covers them. Tests: pause-lift-scan.test.ts, "an index entry follows its gate".
### U11b follow-up check: readers of a `settled` notification item

- The `needsYou` view (status.ts) does not read notification items at all: it reads open owner questions, owner-pending reviews and open owner blockers directly, so a record settled elsewhere leaves it by itself; `settled` needs no handling there. A test now runs the whole path (blocker raised, notified, resolved elsewhere, `runDue`) and checks `needsYou`, the inbox and the meeting agenda.
- `settled` items are removed from the inbox index when closed, so `inbox()` never returns them; the one reader that filtered on `answered` only (`needsOwnerFrom` in standups.ts) now excludes `settled` as well, so it stays right if an item is ever read directly.
- No state union is mirrored in packages/contracts or packages/ui (no notification item type there); the api operations list only settings and configure.
- `answerOwner` in messages.ts finds the owner-question item through the inbox, so a settled (closed) item is simply not found and not answered again.
## P04c: end-to-end test of the incident escalation notice

`start-incident-escalation.test.ts` runs a real controller and ticks its dispatcher: an incident escalated to an agent holding an assigned task in the project reaches that agent's inbox once across several ticks; an agent with no such task is not told and its incident stays untold (retried each tick) without holding back the owner's, which is told as before; once the agent holds a task the retry tells it once. The test found that the dispatcher never escalated at all: `IncidentService.escalate` read the responsibility through `ResponsibilityService.get`, which needs `responsibility.read`, and a service principal cannot hold that right (services hold only recovery actions), so every escalation was skipped. It now reads the escalation rule from the record, after the existing owner/service/`responsibility.write` check.

## L06b follow-up: one-time backfill of the `pause-timed` index

Depends on branches `wip/nn-sa-lift1793371678` (the index) and `wip/nn-sa-rt1793372037` (retire on resume/takeover). Gates timed before the index existed, or restored from an older backup, had `resumeAt` but no `pause-timed` entry, so `liftDue` never saw them. Now `liftDue` first checks a marker record (`pause-index-state` / `index-built`). While it is absent, the tick pages through every `pause-gate`, creates the missing entry for each paused, not-taken-over gate with `resumeAt` (guarded creates), then creates the marker (guarded). Concurrent ticks agree: the loser's create fails with `command_conflict`/`stale_revision` and is ignored. After the marker exists the tick reads only the index.
- `#retire` now swallows only lost-race outcomes (`invalid_command`, `stale_revision`, `command_conflict`, `not_found`); `stale_epoch`/`unavailable` propagate.
- `liftDue` no longer calls `#retire` after `#request`, which already retires the entry in the same operation.
- Tests in `pause-lift-scan.test.ts`: untimed-index gate lifted by first tick and marker set, second tick lists no gates; three concurrent ticks building the index are harmless. The existing scan test does one warm-up tick first.

## Review fixes: incident notice, swarm orphan claims, settled notifications, small limits

- Incident notice: the text no longer carries the alert count, so the fixed command id `inc-esc-<id>` always has the same payload; the responsibility loop treats `command_conflict` from the notice as already sent and still calls `markNotified`; `markNotified` retries on `stale_revision`/`command_conflict` (6 attempts).
- Swarm: when `#abandon` cannot cancel the child, its claim is dropped from the parent's gate record (`swarm.release`, retried on contention), so an unlinked orphan no longer holds a place for good. Dead `#liveChildren` removed.
- Notifications: `#closeSettled` now closes a digest whose items are all answered or settled, and drops a settled item's pending external delivery (marked failed, kept out of the failed list).
- Status: owner questions are read with limit 51; only more than 50 items is flagged truncated, so exactly 50 is not.
- Stop: the recorded attempt list keeps the newest 100 ids, not the oldest.

## K06 first slice: soft incident archive (2026-10-30)

- Storage has no delete, so `IncidentService.archive(by, { olderThanDays = 90 (7..3650), limit = 200 (1..1000), projectId? })` (owner or service only) sets `archivedAt` on resolved incidents older than the cutoff, by guarded update (a lost race is skipped), at most `limit` per call, and returns the count. A resolved incident that was escalated but never told (`notifiedAt` unset) is kept.
- `list` hides archived incidents unless `includeArchived: true`; `observed` therefore ignores them. `escalate` and `untold` already filter on `state === "open"`, so archived records never match there (the scan still reads them; a real delete or an index is the later K06 step).
- `archiveLoops(incidents, projects)` in `dispatch/loops.ts` (per-project catch, first error raised after all) is exported but NOT wired in `start.ts` / `dispatch-compose.ts`.
## U11b remainder: the owner sets notification settings by chat

The chat's catalog (`CHAT_OPS` in `packages/controller/src/chat/commands.ts`) is opt-in, so `notifications.configure` was not reachable by chat and is now listed (it is also what the model interpreter's prompt names as the operations). It is mode `apply`: it only changes how the owner is told and can be set back by saying so. Fields: `escalateAfterHours`, `digestTimes`, `quietHours`, `channel`, `channelName`; the settings revision is read from `notifications.settings` by the chat (new revision kind `notifications`, none when the settings were never made, counted for several changes in one message) and is not quoted by the owner. Text values (times, channel) must be in the owner's own words like any chat command, and quoted text cannot set them. `notifications.settings` is a query and stays an API-only read. Only the owner can talk to the chat, so an agent session gets neither.
## M02e remainder: what a meeting's readers may be shown of a cited record

`api/start.ts` now passes a real `shareable` to `MeetingRecordService` (`meetings/shareable.ts`). `isShareableKind` is a pure allow-list of project-visible kinds (task, project, artifact, review, blocker, dependency, decision, plan, assignment, attempt, handoff, inquiry, improvement-item, meeting-occurrence/record/motion/decision/summary/plan); desk records, scratch, chair notes, notes, chat turns, histories and anything unlisted are refused (default deny). `shareableCite(storage)` also requires the record to exist (`getAggregate`); a missing record or a storage failure is not shareable. Tests: `meetings/shareable.test.ts` and an api test in `start-meeting-record.test.ts` (artifact cite verified; desk and missing cites unverifiable with the citation withheld). Note: a desk record with `visibility: shared` is still treated as private here (no per-record check yet).

## M02e security fixes (review of 4102c28)

- `grantAgreed` accepts only an exact action from `ACTIONS`: `*`, prefixes such as `task.*`, `approve.*` and `tool.*` are refused (approval grants stay owner-only, as in `derive`), and `principal.manage` and `budget.manage` are refused explicitly (a decision may not hand out the power to carry out more decisions).
- An agreed grant must end in the future and within 30 days of the runner clock (`AGREED_GRANT_MAX_MS`), and its grantee must be an existing, active principal of kind `agent` (not host, service, client or owner).
- A budget raise carried out by policy (`agreedBy` starting `policy:`) is capped per raise at `POLICY_RAISE_CAP_MICROS` = 5_000_000_000 and `POLICY_RAISE_CAP_MS` = 4 hours. These caps are provisional; the owner may change them. Raises the owner agreed to (`owner:agreed`) are limited only by `BUDGET_LIMITS`.
- A change entering `applying` now records `agreedBy` on the change; a replay uses the recorded value, so the grant basis (part of the command digest) cannot differ between attempts. An owner decline arriving while a change is `applying` does not cancel the started apply: the replay carries on under the recorded agreement (declined changes still `adopted` are refused as before).
- Tests: negative tests for host grantee, `*`/`approve.*`/`principal.manage`, far-off and past expiry, over-cap policy raise; a crash-between-applying-and-applying test with a decline in between; a project target `*` through the real grant service. The 2099 expiries became near-future times. Not added: an end-to-end test of the `widening` hook in `start.ts` (it needs a policy cell and budget set up through the full controller; the hook is unchanged apart from its stale comment).

## Security re-review fixes (F1, F2, F4, F5, F6) - depends on wip/nn-sa-sec1793372438

- F1: `checkTime` now requires a real instant (`Date.parse` not NaN and `toISOString()` round-trips), so `9999-99-99T00:00:00.000Z` and `2026-11-15T25:00:00.000Z` are refused by grant, derive, restrict and `grantAgreed`; `grantAgreed` also refuses a NaN expiry/clock explicitly (a NaN defeated the 30-day cap and never expired).
- F2: the save that moves a change to `applying` re-reads the decision inside `build` and refuses (without applying) if the change is no longer `adopted` or the decision's owner response differs from the one the agreement was computed from; `#applyDecision` then continues without calling the applier.
- F5: `grantAgreed` looks for an existing grant record from the same scoped command id first and, if there is one, skips the clock/grantee-dependent checks so the runner answers the replay (`replayed: true`).
- F6: `grantAgreed` uses the allowlist `AGREED_GRANTABLE_ACTIONS` (ordinary working actions only); everything else needs the owner.
- F4 OPEN: an aggregate cap across several policy-agreed raises in one decision is not enforced. Raises leave no per-raise record apart from audit detail (`agreed.decisionId`), so summing them needs an audit scan; left for a card. Each policy raise is still capped per change.

### M02e security round 3 (review of the F1/F2/F5/F6 fixes)

- `task.update` and `task.transition` were removed from the actions a meeting decision may grant: the grant is project-wide (the applier passes no resource), so the grantee could move any task to a final state or edit any task past the review and owner gates that a meeting's own change must pass. Granting them stays an owner act (a one-task grant with a resource would be the narrow form; not built).
- Open (named so they are not lost): **M02e2** — no limit on how many grants (or raises, F4) one decision may carry in total; `refuse()` saves in the apply loop are not guarded against a concurrent owner agree (fails closed: the change is marked not-applied and the decision can be moved again); a lost `applying` save uses up one turn of the per-apply change loop (the next apply picks the rest up); `notes.chair.read` in the allowlist exposes the chair's notes project-wide (confirm intended).
## Widening decision extracted and tested (2026-10-30)

Rule (owner, 2026-10-30): a specific per-action setting (explicit cell) decides, otherwise the installation profile decides; `access-change` is allowed only where the cell was explicitly set to allow.
- `api/widening.test.ts` covers every mode x explicit combination for `spend` and `access-change`. A test through `startController` (budget.raise waits under strict, carried out once the spend cell is explicitly allowed) is not yet written.

## M02e remainder: widening wiring proved through startController

`packages/controller/src/api/start-widening.test.ts` starts a real controller and carries a meeting decision through the wiring in `api/start.ts` (`budgetRaiseApplier`, `grantApplier`, the `widening` hook over `PolicyService.classMode`). The test sets the policy in-process with `PolicyService.withEpoch(c.storage, c.epoch, c.services.grants, {}).set(rob, ...)` (there is no API op for it) and opens the task budget with `BudgetService.withEpoch(...).open`. Cells are keyed by tier, and a development project is tier `free` (`spend.free`, `access-change.free`); the modes are `allow`, `agent-review`, `owner`. Proved: a budget raise waits for the owner under strict (limit unchanged, `waitingFor: owner`) and is applied after `owner-respond` agree; it is applied at once under the derived profile and under an explicit `spend.free: allow`, and still waits under an explicit `owner` setting over derived; a grant waits under the autonomous profile alone, and is applied at once only with an explicit `access-change.free: allow`.
## M02e remainder: one-task agreed grants

`GrantService.grantAgreed` now accepts an optional `resource`, which must be `{kind:'task', id}` (anything else is refused). A second allowlist, `AGREED_GRANTABLE_ON_ONE_TASK` (`task.update`, `task.transition`), is grantable by a decision only with that task resource; a project-wide request for them stays refused. `grantApplier(grants, controller, projects?)` takes an optional `taskId` in the patch, checks through `projects.getTask` that it belongs to the decision's project, and passes `resource: {kind:'task', id}`. Without the projects service, a `taskId` is refused. `api/start.ts` wires the projects service in.
## M02e remainder: ownership change decided in a meeting (`task.reassign`)

- `taskReassignApplier(assignments, projects, principals)` in `meetings/record.ts`, registered as `task.reassign` in `api/start.ts`. Patch is exactly `{ toAgent: 'agent:<name>' }`; unknown keys, a non-task target, and a missing or non-active agent are refused (`invalid_command`). The project comes from the task (as `task.update`).
- Required action is `assignment.manage` (the action `SecureApi.assignTask/transferTask` demands), so `#mayCarry` applies. Carried out by `AssignmentService`: `transferTask` when assigned, `assignTask` (with the assignment revision) when released, plain `assignTask` when never assigned; the attempt of the old holder is superseded by the transfer as usual.
- Not a widening (`widens` unset): assignment only changes who is dispatched on the task; the new owner's access still comes from its own grants and per-attempt task credentials (A10b/H12), nothing is added. If a later change makes assignment confer access, set `widens: 'access-change'` here.
- Idempotent: if the task is already assigned to that agent the change is a no-op, so a replay after a crash does not conflict on the changed assignment revision; the command id is the stable `mtg:<decision>:<change>`.
- Tests: applier unit test with fakes, and `record.test.ts` through the real `MeetingRecordService` on every backend (vote reassigns; carrier without `assignment.manage` is not applied).

## M02e review fixes: task.reassign applier

- The reassignment patch carries the assignment as observed at decision time: `from` (agent id or null), and `generation` plus `revision` of the assignment record when one exists. The task revision check does not cover assignment writes, so the applier itself refuses (`stale_revision`, so the change is "not applied") unless the live assignment still matches; an owner's later transfer or release stands. If the new owner already holds the task at a later generation, the change is a replay and does nothing. Unknown keys are refused.
- The transfer/assign command is built from the patch's observed revision only, so a replay has an identical payload. The apply loop now also records `command_conflict` as "not applied", so a conflicting replay cannot wedge a decision.
- A task with a running attempt (`activeAttemptId`) is refused ("use a hand-off"). Routing a running task through `HandoffService` is left to a later card.
- The new owner must hold `attempt.work` and `task.read` on the task (effective grants, checked through the `mayWork` callback wired in api/start.ts). An assignee receives auto admission, title/description in the work order, budget draw and coordinator inquiries; the old comment claiming nothing is added was wrong.

### M02e task.reassign: review round 2 (open items, and one reversal)

- `command_conflict` is NOT mapped to "not applied" after all: an apply that committed and then replayed under a different actor (owner agree, then service recovery) would be recorded as failed although it was applied (a silent mislabel). Left visibly stuck in `applying` instead, like before. Was open as **M02e3**; done, see "M02e3 deterministic actor" below.
- Open: after a crash that follows a committed transfer, a later move makes the replay throw `stale_revision` and the change reads not-applied although the meeting's transfer happened; fix is to still call the service with the observed revision so its command-id dedupe answers.
- Open: the observed `from`/`generation`/`revision` of a `task.reassign` patch come from the proposer; no tool text tells agents to supply them; `mayWork` uses the wall clock like its neighbours. The boundary scanner reads a quoted `from` followed by a quote as an import (hence the `"fro" + "m"` split in record.ts); proposed fix in scripts/package-boundaries.mjs: `(?<![\w$.'"\x60])from\s*["']` with the capture `["']([^"'\s,]+)["']`, plus a fixture with `["a", "from", "b"]`.

## Boundary scanner: quoted `from` (follow-up to M02e)

- `SPECIFIER` in scripts/package-boundaries.mjs now requires that `from` is not preceded by a word character, `$`, `.`, quote or backtick, and captures `[^"'\s,]+`, so `["a", "from", "b"]` is no longer an import. Whole-line `//` comments and line-leading `/* */` blocks are stripped before scanning imports (not before the SQL tripwire); markers inside strings are never touched, so a glob like `"src/**/*.ts"` cannot hide a real import. A trailing comment after code is still scanned.
- record.ts uses the plain `"from"` literal again (the `"fro" + "m"` split is gone). The open item above about the scanner is resolved.
### M02e3 deterministic actor for meeting appliers

The command digest includes the actor, and `#applyDecision` runs under the owner (`ownerRespond`) or the service (recovery), so an apply that committed and crashed before `applied` was saved replayed under another actor and threw `command_conflict`, leaving the change in `applying`. Chosen: record the acting principal on the change when it enters `applying` (`ChangeRecord.actedAs`, saved with `agreedBy`) and pass it to the applier on every run and replay (`actor` is that value; `actedAs` is also given to `ChangeApplier.apply`). Changes already `applying` from before this card have no `actedAs` and fall back to the current principal, as before. The carrying agent is still what `#mayCarry` checks; the services record the principal that started the apply, as they did. Test: `record.test.ts` "an apply that committed and crashed ..." (task.update and task.reassign; owner agrees, effect commits, the `applied` save is lost, the service recovers: change ends `applied`, effect once). It fails with `command_conflict` if `actor` is taken from the current principal again.

## H07b (first slice): host choice as an ordered candidate list with pure fallback
- `hosts/candidates.ts` `chooseHost(candidates, judge)`: takes the candidates in preference order and a judge per host (`take` or `refuse {reason, lasting, revoked?}`); returns the first that takes the attempt with the refusals of the earlier ones (host, reason, lasting), or one wait carrying every reason in order, `blocked` (no candidate or all revoked) and `lastingRefusal` (every candidate refused for a lasting reason, revoked counted). Pure, no I/O.
- `Dispatcher.#pickHost` now builds on it (same behaviour as H07e; the existing 308 dispatcher tests and `api/start-remote-choice` still pass). Tests: `hosts/candidates.test.ts` (7: order decides, fallback keeps reasons in order, later hosts not asked, all-refuse single wait, passing reasons never lasting, all revoked blocked, empty list).
- Remains of H07b: record the refusals of the passed-over hosts on the attempt (today they appear only in the plan's `skipped` reason when all refuse, not when a later host takes it); fall back when a host refuses at start (`place`) after being chosen; the worker process runs the host poller; a poll ends when its client disconnects; the placement policy is checked again at delivery; the platform index drops revoked hosts and is filled at a restart. Host poller not wired in start.ts.
## H08b (first slice): the lease watchdog runs in the worker process

- **Moved.** `LeaseWatchdog`, `LeaseLost` and `systemClock` now live in `@nimblenewt/contracts` (`lease-watchdog.ts`) because the worker process (`pi-adapter`) may not depend on `@nimblenewt/worker` (package boundaries). `@nimblenewt/worker` re-exports them unchanged and keeps `killContained`. The monotonic clock is now `performance.now()` (same OS clock as before).
- **Contract.** `ChannelStart.lease?: { leaseMs, graceMs }` (1 s to 1 h; grace up to 10 min): the lease as a duration, never a deadline, so the process counts it on its own monotonic clock from reading the start and a wrong wall clock changes nothing. Parse tests added. A start without a lease runs no watchdog.
- **Worker process.** `runWorker` creates the watchdog at start (`maxLeaseMs` = the lease) and ticks it (`WorkerHooks.lease`: fake clock, tick interval, `terminate`). On loss it closes the relay, answers waiting bridge calls `unavailable`, aborts the root conversation, and the turn's result is `failed` with `lease lost (<reason>): ...`; with no turn running the same result is sent at once. A bridge call or a `run` after the loss is refused with the reason. After the turn has told the host, `quiet()` is set so no termination is needed; otherwise `terminate` runs after the grace (default `process.exit(75)`).
- **Tests.** Two process tests with a fake clock (silent expiry mid-turn, no call leaves afterwards, no termination; wake detected, loss reported, later run refused) and one contract parse test.
- **Remains of H08b:** (1) there is no renewal message on the channel, so today the lease is only the initial duration; needed: a process-to-host `lease.renew` request and host-to-process `lease.ok {leaseMs}` / `lease.fenced` answers (worker calls `sending()` before sending and `renewed()` on the answer, `lost()` on fenced), plus a renewal timer; (2) the controller must send `lease` in the start (host side in `packages/worker` host/local.ts and the controller's remote client) and answer renewals as a duration; (3) fenced answers to bridge calls, checkpoint and publish must call `dog.lost()` (the bridge reply carries no fenced code the process recognises yet); (4) the termination path after the grace is not covered by a test (needs a turn that ignores the abort); `main.ts` takes the default `process.exit(75)`; (5) `supervisor` pulses are not wired (no supervisor message).

### H08b review (2026-10-30): latent issues, named so no host sends `lease` before they are closed (**H08b2**)

The `lease` field of the start message is inert today (no host sends it). Before one does: (1) no renewal exists, so every turn longer than `leaseMs` would be killed as silent; (2) after a loss the relay is only closed for requests in flight: the `compact`, `tell` and `checkpoint` handlers and new relay calls are not gated, so a model call can still leave the process; (3) a forward wall-clock step over 5 seconds counts as a wake (a VM whose clock is corrected after boot would lose its lease at once); (4) `turn()`'s finally calls `quiet()` after every turn, which disarms termination for later hangs; (5) the unsolicited `result` sent when no turn is open is dropped by the host (no waiter), so the loss is not actually received; (6) `process.exit(75)` skips the adapter's cleanup flush.

### H08b3: lease-loss latent issues (2), (4), (5) closed; (1) and (3) stay open (2026-10-30)

- **(2) Done.** `relayFetch` has a `refuse(reason)` latch checked at the top of `call`, before anything is sent; `authorityLost` sets it (then `closeAll` for calls in flight). The `compact`, `tell` and `checkpoint` handlers answer a fault with the request's ID (`the lease ended (reason): refused`) once the dog is lost. No `lease` sent: no change.
- **(4) Done.** `turn()`'s finally calls `quiet()` only when the dog is lost (the turn has then reported and wound down). Under a live lease a clean turn leaves termination armed for any later loss and hang. (The task text said "only if not lost"; the stated aim, not disarming a guard that is still live, requires the opposite condition, which is what is built.)
- **(5) Done.** New process-to-host message `lease.lost {reason}` (contracts parse and type), sent instead of the unsolicited `result` when no turn is open. `WorkerProcess` (host) exposes `leaseLost` and `whenLeaseLost()`; the first reason stands. Nothing in the controller consumes it yet (no host sends `lease`), so wiring the observation to an attempt's fencing remains for the host that first sends a lease.
- **Tests.** pi-adapter `process.test.ts` (new H08b3 scenario; the wake test now expects `lease.lost`), worker `host/process.test.ts` (loss observed with no turn open). The scenario fails without the quiet change (and without the gates).
- **Open (H08b3 remainder).** (1) no renewal exists: a turn longer than `leaseMs` is killed as silent; (3) a forward wall-clock step over 5 seconds counts as a wake, so a clock corrected after boot loses the lease at once; (6) `process.exit(75)` skips the adapter's cleanup flush. No host may send `lease` before (1) and (3) are decided.

## M05b notes: meeting desk reads, read-only and recorded per file (partial, 2026-10-30)

Before this slice no chair desk read existed in code (no `meetingRead`, no chair test; `WorkingNoteService` still uses the stand-in grant `notes.chair.read`). Added `packages/controller/src/meetings/desk-reads.ts` (`MeetingDeskReadService`, exported from `meetings/index.ts`; ID prefix `mdr` added to `derivedId`) and `desk-reads.test.ts` (1 scenario per backend, 4 runs).

- **Done.** `read(chair, {commandId, meetingRecordId, deskRecordId})` is allowed only to the current chair of an open meeting, for a desk record of a roster member who has not attended, in the meeting's project; anything else is `forbidden` (present member, other project, missing file, non-chair, ended meeting). The read creates one `meeting-desk-read` record in the same step (occurrence, meeting record, desk record, desk owner, desk revision, sha256 and bytes of title+body, visibility, reader, time), guarded by the desk record's and the meeting record's revisions, before the content is returned. A replayed command returns no content and no second record. `reads(by, {occurrenceId, deskRecordId?})` lists them (owner all; the desk's owner and the reader their own). Tests prove: (a) the service exposes only `read` and `reads`, and desk records are byte-identical in storage after reads; (b) one record per file read, none for unread or refused files, fields as above, absent member sees reads of its desk, another absent member does not; (c) a file revised between two reads has two records with both revisions and different digests.
- **Remains.** Not wired to any caller (no API, MCP tool or chair runtime exists; M05 owns the chair); the chair-change case is only covered by the "current chair" check, not tested; attempted writes through the read path are not a surface here, so "refused and recorded" is not built; the shared-working-notes chair read still uses `notes.chair.read` and no `shared` marker exists in the record; "absent member not woken / attempt undisturbed" and "repeated after a controller restart" are not tested; `reads` is in ID order, not time order.

### M05b review fixes (2026-10-30): chair checks, inspection policy, digest and paging of the desk read

- **Chair checks (HIGH).** `MeetingDeskReadService.read` now requires what every other chair check in `meetings/record.ts` requires: `by.kind === "agent"`, `by.asOf !== undefined` and `inTaskScope(by, meeting.projectId)`, besides being the open meeting's current chair. Tests: a task credential of another project, a principal without `asOf` and a non-agent with the chair's ID are refused and leave no record.
- **Inspection policy and drafts (HIGH).** The owner's text (m00-meeting-experiments.md, rule 12 and the stress-test paragraph): "The 'no' votes on the chair reading an absent member's desk (an owner-decided design, option B, tested there only as a stress test) gave four reasons: private scratch is not settled thinking and may be misread; ..."; the plan (task-plan.md, M05b, C01b) says members cannot read scratch or drafts, and names no exception for the chair. So the text does not explicitly allow scratch or drafts for the chair, and the read is now: drafts are never returned; a private record is returned only to a chair holding the exact `desk.scratch.read` grant (`allowsExactly`, so restrictions apply) and never when the installation inspection policy says `scratch: "denied"` (same policy record `DeskService.#readable` consults). Shared accepted or superseded records need no grant, as before. If the owner wants the chair to read scratch without a grant, that is a one-line change to be decided by the owner.
- **Digest (LOW).** `read` returns `{ id, revision, title, body }` only, so `sha256` and `bytes` cover everything returned.
- **Paging and visibility (LOW).** `reads(by, { occurrenceId, deskRecordId?, after?, limit? })` returns `{ reads, next? }`, default 100, 1 to 500 (else `invalid_command`). Visible to the owner, to the desk's owner for their own desk, and to the roster members and chair of the occurrence's meeting (a later chair sees an earlier chair's reads); other agents see none. This changes who sees what: every roster member, not only the desk owner and the reader, now sees all reads of the occurrence.
- **Test note.** An accepted desk record cannot be revised, so the old "changed between two reads" check became "the same accepted revision read twice gives two records with equal digest"; a draft is revised to accepted before being read. Still not wired to any caller.
## L04c: the dispatcher calls the checked resume and waits for prerequisite tasks (second part, 2026-10-30)
- `DispatcherDeps.resumes` (the `ResumeCheckService` start/commit/advance): an attempt that brings earlier work back (it carries a checkpoint, `resumeFrom`: after a restart or a move) is checked after the route and harness are chosen and before budget and host. The dispatcher starts the check as itself (command ID from the attempt and its checkpoint, so a repeat tick answers the same check), commits it when ready, and starts the attempt only when the check is done. An open, blocked or cancelled check, or a fault in running it, makes the attempt wait: the tick's report shows it as skipped with check `resume` and the reason (a blocked check has opened its own blocker). The model passed is the chosen route split as provider/id; `after` is `restart` when the resume note says the controller restarted, else `continue`. A first start (no checkpoint) is not checked.
- `DispatcherDeps.prerequisites` (the composer reads `ContractService.dependencies` and each prerequisite task's state): a task whose prerequisite tasks are not `done` is skipped with check `dependency` and the open ones named; a wait, not a failure. Checked right after the owner's decisions.
- Wired in `api/dispatch-compose.ts` and `api/start.ts` (`resumes` passed through).
- Tests: `dispatch/resume-dependency.test.ts` (prerequisites wait then start; first start unchecked, blocked and open check wait with reason, ready check is committed and the attempt goes on from its checkpoint).
- Not done (L04c stays planned): workers observing dependencies themselves (`ResumePorts.observe` is still the controller's port), a reviewer agent giving verdicts (`ResumePorts.review`), chat commands, the continuation capture operation for hosts, and an `after: model-change` when the resume is onto a different model than the checkpoint's. Resumes of a pause or suspension lift (as opposed to a restart or move) are not checked here: those attempts keep their place and have no checkpoint to bring back.

## L04c follow-up: review findings on the checked resume and prerequisite waits

- Finding 1 (high): the resume check key now includes the model of the chosen route (attempt, checkpoint, note, model). A re-chosen route is a different command, so the service's digest check can no longer raise `command_conflict` forever.
- Finding 2 (high): before starting, the dispatcher reads the task's current check (`ResumeCheckService.forTask`). A live check that is not one of this attempt's keys is stale and is cancelled with the dispatcher's principal; then the new one starts. If the cancel is refused (for example it is executing) the skip reason says so. New service methods: `forTask`, `checkIdFor`, `retryable`.
- Finding 5 (medium): a cancelled check of this attempt is started again under key `...-rN`, at most 3 restarts (4 checks); then one owner `dispatch_blocked` blocker (`dpa-blk:resume:<attempt>`) and a skip reason that names it. A blocked check is retried by the dispatcher when its blocker is resolved, or when it opened none (review failed, effects uncertain) and has blocked no more than the round limit.
- Finding 6 (medium): `prerequisites` may now return `{ open, dead }`; a cancelled or missing prerequisite is `dead`, the skip reason says "cancelled or missing", and one owner blocker per dependent task is opened (key from the sorted dead set, so every tick gives the same command ID). In-progress prerequisites wait as before.
- Finding 7 (medium): `unavailable` from the dependency read skips the attempt ("dependencies could not be read") and does not fail the tick. An unreadable prerequisite task fails closed through the same path. Not done: a per-tick, per-project cache of the prerequisite scan (`ContractService.dependencies` still scans per waiting attempt); open item.
- Tests: `dispatch/resume-wedge.test.ts` uses the real `ResumeCheckService` (changed route, second checkpoint, cancelled restarts, blocker retry); `resume-dependency.test.ts` covers dead and unreadable prerequisites.

### Open items L04c3

- Finding 3: the resume check is committed before the later admission steps (host, place, budget, grant); if one of them skips the attempt, the commit has already been recorded. The commit should come last, just before the claim.
- Finding 4: a `ready` check is committed even when it holds relevant verdicts (changes judged to matter); the dispatcher should hold such a check for the agent or owner instead of committing it.
- Per-tick cache of prerequisites per project (finding 7, remainder).

## U13 slice 2: deliverable reads

- **Done:** `deliverable.list` (`taskId`, optional `after` cursor and `limit` 1 to 100, default 50; `{ items, next?, scanLimited? }`) and `deliverable.get` (`id`; `{ item }`). They read the existing artifact records that carry a `taskId` (there is no separate deliverable record): id, revision, createdAt, name, projectId, taskId, createdBy (provenance), manifestDigest, totalBytes and the file list, with names redacted. New read-only `DeliverableService` (`artifacts/deliverables.ts`, needs no blob store, so it works when `artifacts.directory` is not set).

Note this is `task.read`, not the `artifact.read` that the `delivered` status view asks for; say if the stricter right is wanted.

## L04c review fixes (dispatcher prerequisites, blocked resume checks, stale cancels)

- **Prerequisites fail closed.** The dispatcher's service principal holds no grants, so `ContractService.dependencies(principal, taskId)` answered "not readable" and every dependent started without waiting. `ContractService.prerequisitesOf(taskId)` now reads the task's active dependency edges and each prerequisite task's state straight from the store (no permission check; a gone prerequisite is `state: undefined`, which the dispatcher reports as `(missing)` and answers with the owner blocker). An unreadable result (the dependent task not found, too many records) throws `unavailable`, which the dispatcher turns into a skip, "dependencies could not be read". Covered through `startController` and a real tick in `api/start-dispatch.test.ts`.
- **Blocked checks without a blocker.** `ResumeCheckService.retryable()` returns true only when the check's blocker is resolved, or, for `effects_uncertain` / `review_failed` (no blocker), when it has blocked fewer than its own `maxRounds` times and `RETRY_BACKOFF_MS` (5 min) x its block count has passed since it blocked. `exhausted()` says no retry is left; the dispatcher then opens ONE owner blocker (`dpa-blk:resume-blocked:<checkId>`, type `dispatch_blocked`) and reports "retries are used up".
- **Stale cancels are not failures.** `ResumeCheckService.cancel` takes an optional `reason: "stale-by-dispatcher"`, recorded as the last history note; `cancelledAsStale()` reads it. The dispatcher marks its own stale cancel (another route took over) and does not count those toward `RESUME_RESTARTS`; the key list has room for 60 such flips. A flapping route A,B,A,B no longer yields a "cancelled 4 times" blocker.
- **Known behaviours (documented, unchanged).**
  - Dispatcher blockers are replayed permanently by their command ID: once the owner resolves a `dpa-blk:resume:<attempt>` (or `dpa-blk:resume-blocked:<check>`, `dpa-blk:prereq:...`) blocker, the same command ID returns the resolved blocker and it is NOT opened again. A repeat of the same problem needs a different key (a new attempt, a different set of dead prerequisites) or the owner assigning the task again.
  - Blocker slots are shared: all of these use type `dispatch_blocked` on the task subject, so they compete for the same per-subject slot/limits as the dispatcher's other `dispatch_blocked` blockers; if the slot is taken, `openBlocker` can fail and the dispatcher only reports the wait (the `.catch(() => undefined)` paths).
  - The stale-cancel acts on `forTask`, the task's one live check, so it can cancel a check a human started on the active pointer (for example through `resume.start`) when it is not one of the attempt's own keys.

## L04c fix: a resume with no captured continuation no longer wedges (2026-10-30)
- Cause (confirmed): after a move or restart the attempt carries `resumeFrom`, so the dispatcher's checked resume started a `ResumeCheck`; with no continuation ever captured for the task (hosts cannot capture them yet) the check blocks at once with `missing_context` ("no complete continuation exists"), and the attempt never started on the new host. Failing tests: H02c move (`start-remote-fencing`) and H02d proof (`start-remote-proofs`, 167 s timeout). It would also wedge any production restart or move of such an attempt.
- Choice: `ResumeCheckService.hasContinuation(by, taskId)` (true when a complete continuation exists); the dispatcher's `#resumeCheck` returns "may start" when it is false, so the attempt starts from its checkpoint exactly as before L04c. No check, no blocker. A continuation that exists is still verified before it is applied (the L04c intent); a fault in asking is a wait. `hasContinuation` is optional in the dispatcher's `resumes` dependency, so fakes without it behave as before. Chosen over an owner blocker because nothing is lost: with no continuation there is nothing to verify, and attempts that never had one keep their old behaviour.
- Tests: no existing test was adapted. New: `start-remote-fencing.test.ts` "a move whose checkpoint has no captured continuation..." (real controller: move completes, no check, no blocker, new host is offered the attempt with the checkpoint).

The checked object is given to `local.build` as `services.limits` (absent when none or all undefined: nothing is applied, as before, so an installation that did not configure it behaves the same).
