## U13 remainder: activity.explanations pages

`activity.explanations` now takes `after` (a position, the previous `next`) and `limit` (1-100, default 50), validated as `activity.corrections` is, and returns `{ items, next? }`. Without a step, the cursor is a position in the task's index id list (the worker's own explanations in the order written, then retrospective ones) and `ActivityService.explanationsPage` reads only that page's records from storage. A page may be shorter than `limit` when its steps are in an unavailable range; `next` still advances. With a step, the per-step list (via `bySeq`) is sliced. Order without a step is therefore contemporaneous-then-retrospective rather than a global sort by time. The status view still uses the unpaged `explanations()`.

## H12o notes: commit an approved submission exactly once (2026-10-30, partial)

`packages/controller/src/gate/commit-once.ts` (`commitOnce`, `CommitPort`, `MadeCommit`) and `commit-once.test.ts` (4 suites on 4 backends = 16 tests, through the real gate, review and grant services; the existing 36-test gate suite still passes).

- **Done.** `commitOnce(gate, by, port, {requestId, base, tree, message})` runs: (1) a request already recorded as committed answers from the record; (2) the port looks in the checkout for a commit the request already made and, if its parent and tree equal the approved base and tree, records it, even after the 30-minute permit has run out (restart recovery); (3) otherwise it authorizes (same permit on retry), the port commits and the commit is recorded. Command IDs are derived from the request ID, so repeats replay. A found commit with another tree or base is never recorded and gives `review_invalid` ("a new approval is needed"); a found commit for a request that was never authorized is refused; a changed tree, base or message is refused by `authorize` as before.
- **Not done (dependencies H12n and Q01b are not built).** There is no submission record: the A06 commit request stands in as "the submission" (provisional, named in the code). Not built: tying the commit to a submission ID and opening it from `work.end`, a real `CommitPort` over the worker's `GitBridge.commit` (the worker finds its commit by the `NimbleNewt-Request:` trailer the permit already carries) and calling `commitOnce` from the controller's release operation (workspace `release`), and a real-git end-to-end test of a crash between commit and record. The port is tested with an in-memory fake that crashes after committing.
- **Owner question.** Should a submission that was approved but whose commit was made by a different principal (for example the integrator, P10) be recorded by that principal, or always by the author? Provisional: only the requester or the owner may record.

### H12o review fixes (2026-10-30)

- **Concurrency.** `commitOnce` now queues calls per request ID in process; a second concurrent call finds the first's record and returns its commit ID (`alreadyRecorded`). Cross-process exclusion is not provided here: a real `CommitPort` must move HEAD with compare-and-swap (base to new commit only if HEAD is still the base). Documented on `CommitPort`.
- **Recovery by marker, not HEAD.** `CommitPort` gains optional `findByRequest` (trailer in reachable history plus made records for unreferenced commits) and `intend(requestId, tree)`. A real port must write intent before committing and a made record {requestId, sha} before moving HEAD. The service prefers `findByRequest`. The authorize command ID now includes the permit generation (`permitUntil`, "first" before any); the gate still refuses an authorize after an expired permit without a new review, so a full re-approval flow after expiry is not built (it needs the gate to accept a fresh review for the same request).
- **Approval re-check.** New `CommitGateService.approvalStands(by, requestId)` (external approval stands; review must be approved or used, not denied/withdrawn/missing). Recovery asserts state `authorized`, tree equals the approved tree and the approval stands before recording; otherwise `review_invalid` and the commit stays unrecorded. A used review cannot be withdrawn by the review service, so the recovery refusal is tested with a gate stub; the gate method is tested with a real withdrawn review. There is no separate contributor-withdrawal flag in the gate; H05 contributor withdrawal appears as a withdrawn review.
- **Tree check and docs.** The port's `commit` result now carries `tree`; a tree other than the approved one is refused (`review_invalid`) and not recorded. Doc corrected: the record steps are the requester's or the owner's, `authorize` is the requester's only.
- Tests: 4 new suites x 4 backends (commit-once now 32 tests, all pass; the 16 new fail without the fix).

- Writes no longer follow links: each file is opened `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW` (truncated only after the checks), then `fstat` is compared with `lstat` (`sameFile`), `nlink` must be 1 and the real parent must still be the resolved one; a swap is refused as `link_refused`. A refusal on the last file changes no earlier file. A file already holding the markers `- Modes: a landing file keeps its mode (100755 kept; chmod after write); a mode-only change by the agent counts as its work (listed in `kept`, kept when the landing branch changes the content). ## Q01b: submission kinds by role (service slice, 2026-10-30)
- `SubmissionService` (`submissions/submissions.ts`, record kind `submission`, ID `sbm-...` derived from the caller-scoped command ID, so a repeat records once and a reused ID with other content conflicts). `record(by, {taskId, kind, role, ...})` writes one record per submission attempt; `get` reads one (owner, or the agent that made it; others get nothing).
- Kinds and roles (`KIND_ROLES`): code -> author, review -> reviewer, qa -> qa, document -> docs, signoff -> director. The agent must hold the role it names (checked by an injected `rolesOf`, the controller passes `agents.rolesOfPrincipal`), and a role may submit only its own kinds. Owner and non-agent principals are refused (they hold no role); the agent needs `task.read` on the task and, with a task credential, only its own task.

A non-code kind is refused if it carries `base`, `tree` or `patchId` ("makes no commit"); every record has `makesCommit: false`. Review, qa and signoff name a `subject` (a code or document submission of the same task) and copy its `tree`/`patchId`/`artifactDigest`, so a verdict is bound to the exact tree and patch it was given (P09 can compare patch-ids). A document submission names `artifactDigest` (and optionally `artifactId`).

## H12n slice 1: the ending order, records and rules (partial; 2026-10-30)

- **Done** (`packages/controller/src/work-end/`): `WorkEndService` with `request` (agent only, own attempt only; shape checked; one durable ending intent per attempt; the attempt frozen after the intent is written), `complete` (settle, kill hung calls, stage and open the submission, tell, finish; once per attempt, concurrent calls share one run), `drop` (emergency stop), `recover` (restart completes each open ending once) and `get`. The pure rule `overlapOf`: a submit is refused (`SubmitRefused`, carrying the head commit and the overlapping files) only when the base is stale and a changed file was also changed on the landing branch; a plain end is never refused. An owner stop (or an attempt that is no longer live) drops the intent with nothing staged. A killed write call, a failing submission or a controller with no submit port turns the submit into a plain end with a `runtime_hold` blocker and the typed reason `release_failed` / `submit_unavailable` on the record.

A stale base with no overlapping file may submit (the card says refuse only when overlapping).

## H12n slice 1: review fixes (2026-10-30)

- **Steps are recorded as they happen.** The intent record carries `steps` (`settled`, `submitted{submissionId | typed/summary/blocker}`, `told`, `finished`); each is written (revision-checked) right after its effect, and `complete`/`recover` resume from the first undone step. Ports get a stable key per step (`workend:<attempt>:submitted|told|finished`; `submit`, `tell` and `finish` take it as a last argument and must be replay-safe). If the attempt is no longer live but `finished` is recorded (or the run had already begun and nobody stopped the attempt), the ending is recorded `done` with the stored submission, not dropped.
- **Drop racing complete.** Before submit, tell and finish the intent is re-read; `dropped` aborts with no side effect. A drop that lands after a submit keeps the drop but records the submission and says so in `summary`. Record writes retry on a stale revision and annotate a dropped record rather than overwrite it.
- **One runner per intent.** `complete` first writes a claim (`{epoch, instance}`, revision-checked, state `ending`). A claim by another instance in the same or a newer epoch is `unavailable` ("busy", retryable; `recover` skips it); an older epoch's claim is taken over. Record-write command IDs now carry the revision, so a replayed write cannot pass for another instance's.
- **Overlap re-check.** After settle, before submit, `landing` is read again; a new overlap (or an unreadable checkout) ends plainly with the new typed reason `submit_refused` and a blocker.
- **Request replay.** `frozen` is recorded; a replayed request on a still-`requested`, unfrozen intent retries the freeze. A replay whose submit/result/note/message differ is `command_conflict`. The two `release_failed` blockers use distinct keys (`:release_failed:settle`, `:release_failed:submit`).
- Limits: a restart is assumed to bring a higher epoch (a claim by the same epoch but another instance is busy). The "no longer live, never stopped, begun" resume trusts that only this ending ends the attempt. Tests that failed-before were checked by reasoning, not by a clean old-code run.

## H12n: binding the ending to the controller (2026-10-30)

- **Finish with a result.** `DispatcherService.finishWith(by, attemptId, { result, note?, submissionId? })` ends an attempt with the agent's result: `done` and `partial` end it `succeeded`, `blocked` and `abandoned` end it `abandoned`; the summary names the result, the note and the submission. It reuses the dispatcher's one end path (commands derived from the attempt), so a repeat or an already finished attempt does nothing. The task is not touched. Provisional mapping (owner question: should `blocked` open a blocker, as `failed` does?).
- **Ports.** `work-end/ports.ts` `dispatcherEndingPorts` binds `attempts` to the dispatcher as its service principal: `get` (live = not finished), `freeze`, `settle` (cancel in flight, then the calls recorded `cancelled` or `uncertain` are the killed ones, `write` = the catalogue did not call them read-only) and `finish`. Before the dispatcher exists a call says `unavailable`.
- **Binding.** `start.ts` builds the `WorkEndService` before the API and the stop service (the dispatcher is reached lazily). `landing` returns `undefined` and `submit` is unbound, so `work.end { submit: true }` is refused as `unavailable` (nothing recorded) until Q01b lands; a plain end works. `services.workEnd` is exposed.
- **Operation.** `work.end` (agent only; the service answers `not_found` for an unknown attempt and another agent's alike; the owner gets `forbidden`; a repeat with the same content is the recorded ending, with different content `command_conflict`). The task credential's own task is not compared with the attempt's task; the attempt's agent is.
- **Stops.** `dispatchStopPorts` takes an `ending` hook; the terminate step calls `drop` before it stops each attempt (`owner_stop`, or `emergency_stop` for Force Stop). A stop still in preparation leaves the intent alone (the attempt keeps settling).
- **Recovery.** `recover()` runs once at start-up (when a dispatcher exists) and as the sweep `workend.complete` in every tick, which completes open intents. An attempt that was running when the controller closed is ended by the shutdown itself, so its intent is then dropped as "the attempt ended"; an open intent of a waiting attempt is completed after a restart (test).
- Remaining: `landing` (base and changed files of the checkout) and `submit` (staging and the Q01b submission), the agent tool registration, and a unit test of the `owner_stop` typing through `dispatchStopPorts` (the integration test covers Force Stop).

## H12n: review fixes for the dispatcher binding (2026-10-30)

- **1 (HIGH) the agent's next move no longer loses the ending.** `DispatcherService.onEnd(hook)` is asked at the top of `#end` (every end: the turn completing, a stop, a lost worker, expiry) and `start.ts` binds it to `WorkEndService.resolveOnEnd(attemptId, how)`. A turn that completes after `work.end` runs the whole ending (`complete`: settle, submit, tell) and the attempt ends with the agent's result through `finishWith` (which skips the hook): `blocked` is recorded as `abandoned` with the note, not as a plain success. Any other end (failed, lease) keeps the dispatcher's outcome, tells the agent's message, drops the intent as `attempt_ended` and writes the agent's request into the end's summary. A stop drops it as `owner_stop` / `emergency_stop`. `EndingAttempt.stopped` is now filled: `stop()` records `stopped {by, reason}` on the attempt before it freezes. The sweep's "attempt gone, nothing started" drop is `attempt_ended` (new typed reason), `owner_stop` only for a real stop.
- **2 (HIGH) a stop in preparation stops the ending.** New optional `StopPorts.begin(scope, {force})`, called by `StopService.request` and `force` as soon as the stop is recorded and the scope paused; `dispatchStopPorts` drops the ending of every attempt of the scope then. `WorkEndDeps.paused(taskId)` (bound to `PauseService.isPaused`, so a stop, a suspension or a plain pause on the task, agent, team or installation) makes `request` answer `unavailable`, makes `complete` do nothing (no settle, submit or finish) until the pause is lifted, and `work.end` also refuses an attempt that was stopped. A plain pause leaves the intent for after the resume. `release` from the stop ports lifts the ending's freeze too (the ending was dropped at `begin`).
- **3 (MEDIUM) races.** (a) `finish` takes a `confirm` callback that `finishWith` asks right before `#end` (a drop that landed after the guard makes it return `false`, the attempt is not ended, the run is aborted as dropped). The window between that check and the end's first write remains (no cross-record transaction); a stop that wins it ends the attempt abandoned and the intent shows `done`. (b) the terminate loop skips an attempt whose `stop` answers `not_found` and goes on with the rest.
- **4 (MEDIUM) the freeze is the ending's.** `Frozen.ending` marks it; `release`, `relocate` and a recipe change keep it (`release(by, id, { includeEnding: true })` lifts it, used by the stop ports).
- **5 (MEDIUM) sweep.** `recover` goes through an index of OPEN endings (`work-end-open/open`, written before the intent, pruned of closed ones by `recover`; records from before the index are scanned in once), at most 50 per call; one failing ending is collected and the rest completed, the failures are thrown together at the end (the sweep reports them). `settle` answering `not_found` counts as already settled (port and service).
- **6 (MEDIUM) task scope.** The service answers `not_found` (same as another agent's attempt) when the credential's task is not the attempt's task; tested through `startController`.
- **7 (LOW)** `settle` reports only calls that were running when it began; a `cancelled` call is not a write (no effect yet), an `uncertain` one is unless it was read-only. **9 (LOW)** a `partial` ending ends `succeeded` but does not reset the context overflow counter; only `done` does.
- **10 (LOW, Q01b) owner question left open:** `rolesOfPrincipalIn` returns the global roles whenever the agent holds any non-tool grant in the project. Not changed here; for the owner to decide how project-scoped roles should be read.

## H12n review fixes, round 2 (second review of f079219)

- Fix 1 (dispatcher `#end`): the end is registered in `#endingBy`/`#ending` synchronously, before the end hook is awaited, so a second end of the same attempt (stop vs the sweep's complete, a failed turn) joins the first and `idle()` waits for the hook. The hook is raced against `endHookMs` (option, default 30 s); on timeout the attempt ends with the dispatcher's own outcome, `onError` is told, and the intent is dropped as attempt_ended later. `finishWith` (skipHook) called from inside the hook (complete -> finish) does not join the end waiting for it (would deadlock); it ends the attempt itself.
- Fix 2 (`resolveOnEnd`): when `complete()` does not finish (paused, busy, unavailable) and the agent's result is not `done`, the hook overrides the outcome (`partial` -> succeeded with the overflow count kept, `blocked`/`abandoned` -> abandoned), runs the tell and drops the intent as attempt_ended. The hook result gained `outcome` and `partial`.
- Fix 3 (stop.ts `request`): `begin` is skipped on a replay and when the stop intent is already terminal.
- Fix 4 (dispatcher `stop`): the `stopped` marker is written just before `#end` (after freeze/settle/checkpoint), and `release(includeEnding)` clears it.
- Fix 5: `recover` counts only endings completed or failed against the cap of 50 and rotates its starting point per call; the open-endings index is now 32 shard documents (`work-end-open` `s0..s31`, plus a `scanned` marker) written with up to 24 jittered retries, so concurrent `work.end` calls rarely share a document (the old single `open` doc is ignored; the one-time backfill rescans). The dead `by === "other"` comparison is gone.
- Tests added: hook race/timeout/throw, stopped marker after a failed stop, partial vs done overflow reset, stop replay, blocked+pause, emergency_stop end to end, recover cap with 55 paused endings. Not re-verified against the pre-fix code by running (the new option does not compile there).

## H12n: binding `submit` and `landing` through optional host functions (2026-10-30)
- `StartOptions.stage?(attempt) => {base, tree, patchId, files}` and `StartOptions.landing?(taskId) => Landed | undefined` are the host-provided functions (the workspace host is not composed yet, H12k). Both are unset by default: `landing` then reports the checkout unknown, so `work.end {submit:true}` is refused `unavailable`, exactly as before.
- `stagedSubmit` (work-end/ports.ts) is the `submit` port: it stages through `stage`, refuses (`checkout_changed`, so the ending ends plainly with `release_failed`) if the staged base is not the base that was checked, and records ONE `code` submission in the `author` role through `SubmissionService.record` as the attempt's agent. The command ID is the ending's step key, so a replay records once. Role, ownership of the attempt and project grants are all still checked by the submission service. With `landing` set but no `stage`, a submit ends plainly as `submit_unavailable` with a blocker.
- The freshness checks are untouched (request time: `SubmitRefused`; after settling: typed `submit_refused` plus blocker).
- Found: the dispatcher names an attempt's owner by its bare agent id (it prefixes `agent:`), while the submission service compared the owner id to the principal id (`agent:<id>`). The `attemptOf` port in start.ts now normalizes the owner to `agent:<id>` (same identity, no check weakened).
- `submissions` is now built before `workEnd` in start.ts.
- Tests: start-work-end.test.ts (stub stage/landing: one submission tied to the attempt with base/tree/patch, replay and repeated sweeps stage once, landing moved into the agent's files after the request gives `submit_refused` with blocker, the same at request time is refused, no `stage` gives `submit_unavailable`).

## M02f (part 1): the meeting decision log (2026-10-30)
- `MeetingRecordService` writes one `meeting-decision-log` aggregate (`DecisionLogBody`, record-types.ts) per change that reaches a final state. Its ID and command ID come from decision + change + outcome (`mdl-...`), so a repeat of the apply, a replay after a restart and a late sweep find the line already there. Nothing is ever updated.
- Outcomes: `applied`; `not-applied` (conflict, missing, failed, no applier); `refused` (code `unauthorized` or `gate`, including the policy tightening after the vote); `declined` (owner declined); `overridden` (owner chose an alternative).
- Written by `#logChanges(decisionId)`, which sweeps every final-state change of the decision. It runs at the end of every apply path and after an owner decline or alternative, so a crash between the change saving and the log write is repaired by the next apply (the restart recovery already repeats it). Best effort: a log failure never changes a decision.
- Entry content: kind, target kind, project, decision and change IDs, outcome, code, `decidedBy` (owner / policy / steward (reserved) / none), `agreedBy`, `actedAs`, the widening class and the policy cell (`setting`: `allow` if the policy let it through, `ask` otherwise; for a refusal the hook is asked at log time), SHA-256 of the canonical patch, and counters (`fields`, plus `costMicros`/`computeMs` for `budget.raise`, `action` for `grant.add`). No patch text, summary or reason is kept.
- Behaviour change to note: the final `applied` save now keeps `agreedBy` and `actedAs` on the change (before, the stale pre-start copy lost them); the log reads them there.
- Query `meeting.decisions.log` (owner only; `MeetingRecordService.decisionLog`): filters `kind`, `outcome`, `projectId`; `limit` 1-100 (default 50); `after` is the `next` cursor; ID order (not time order); result `{ item: { entries, next? } }`. Docs regenerated.
- Tests: record.test.ts (all four backends: four outcomes, no content kept, replay and restarted service add nothing, filters, paging, non-owners refused) and api/start-decision-log.test.ts (through startController, including a restart).
- Remaining for M02f: the steward agent for decisions no coded rule covers (it should use `decidedBy: "steward"`, agreedBy `steward:...`); the narrator; chat commands for meetings and a chat reading of the log; learning auto-apply rules from the log (needs production data); time-ordered listing if wanted; the open items from M02e (per-decision limit on grants/raises, aggregate cap, unguarded refuse saves).

## Joined stop and the end-hook suite on slow storage (unhandledRejection on Windows CI)

- Root cause (test): the suite waited a fixed 10 ms for the end hook and asserted `calls === 1`, with `first`/`second` stop promises left unobserved. On slow PostgreSQL (Windows) the hook was not reached in 10 ms, the assertion threw, the suite closed storage, and the still-running stops then rejected ("the storage is closed") with no handler: `unhandledRejection`.
- Production hazard (real, smaller): a second `stop()` that joined an end in progress still wrote the stopped marker via `#update` first, a write that could land after the end finished or storage closed, and a marker write failing because the attempt ended meanwhile rejected the stop. A joined stop now writes nothing; a marker write failure on an already ended attempt is swallowed.
- Test: handlers attach at once, hook reached by polling, joined stop asserted to leave the dispatch record revision unchanged (fails without the fix on all four backends), both stops asserted to resolve.
## M02f (part 2): decision log review fixes (2026-10-30)
- Lost lines (MEDIUM): a per-project `meeting-decision-unlogged` index (`UnloggedIndexBody`) gets the decision ID in the same save that creates an in-scope adopted decision with changes. `#logChanges` removes it once every change is final and every line exists. `MeetingRecordService.sweep` (already run by the `meeting-records.sweep` loop through `recordLoops`, so no new registration) now also calls `#sweepLog`: up to 20 decisions per call, round-robin via a `from` cursor in the index so decisions waiting for the owner do not starve the rest; the result gains `logChecked`. Decisions made before this change are not in the index (a repeat of apply still logs them).
- One failing change (MEDIUM): `#applyDecision` wraps the change loop in try/finally, so the lines of finished changes are written even when a later applier throws a plain error; `#logChanges` never throws, so a log failure cannot change a decision result.
- Policy cell and `decidedBy` (LOW/MED): `ChangeRecord.setting` keeps the widening cell read when a change is started or refused; the log reads it there (no policy call at logging time; owner declines have none). An owner-agreed change refused with `unauthorized` is logged `decidedBy: owner`, `agreedBy: owner:agreed`, `code: rights_withdrawn`. A plain team vote that widens nothing (`policy:none`) is `decidedBy: vote`. Types and `meeting.decisions.log` docs updated.
- Reader (LOW): a task-scoped owner credential is refused (`taskScope !== undefined`, as policy-edit.ts). At most 20 storage reads per call (pages of 100, option `logScan` for tuning/tests); an early stop returns `scanLimited: true` and `next`. The existence check precedes building the body.
- Tests (record.test.ts, all backends): crash simulation by a storage proxy that fails one log write (owner decline, last change applied), sweep fills the gap once; c1 applied with c2 throwing; overridden, not-applied (conflict), vote, refused-with-cell-at-decision-time, rights_withdrawn, task-scoped owner, scan limit.
## U13 remainder: overview attention list `status.attention` (2026-10-30, partial)

- **Done.** New read operation `status.attention` (`StatusService.attention`): a paged list of what in the overview needs a person's eye. Kinds: `paused_assignee` (a task with an assigned owner and a pause gate; detail lists the gates), `unreachable_worker` (the owner's work was reported by a host that is revoked or not heard from within the host freshness window; detail has `hostId` and `reason` `revoked`/`quiet`), `uncertain_tool_result` (an MCP call with `uncertain` or no recorded outcome; detail has call id, server, capability, outcome, revisions). Filters: `projectId`, `taskId`, `agentId` (owner of record; for tool calls the caller), `state` (the TASK's state), `kind`, `since` (exclusive) and `until` (inclusive) on each item's `at` (pause time, falling back to the task's last change; last sign of work; call time). `limit` 1-100 default 50, `after` cursor. Result `{ observedAt, items, next?, scanLimited? }`.
- **Rights, like the neighbours.** Pauses and workers need what `status.ask` task/overview need to see ownership (owner, `assignment.read`/`assignment.manage`, or the assigned agent itself); tool results need what the `tools` view needs (owner, `history.read` in the project, or `attempt.work` on the task); the task must be readable (`task.read`). A task credential may ask only with its own `taskId`. Without a project or task only the owner may ask (`forbidden`). An agent filter never matches what the caller cannot see. Read only: nothing is written, no replay concern; the host-quiet test is shared with the status `execution` view (`#hostProblem`).
- **Paging and bounds.** Tasks in ID order, each task's items in a fixed order (paused, unreachable, then calls by call ID). The cursor names the last item handed out (`taskId|rank|id`), so it survives items appearing or resolving between pages (calls resume with the storage `afterId`). The scan reads at most `scanPages x scanPageSize` records (tasks plus calls); when that runs out, or one task's call list exceeds `scanPages` pages, `scanLimited` is set and `next` continues. Rows are never skipped or repeated.
- **Tests.** `status/status.test.ts` suite "the attention list ..." x 4 backends (120 tests in the file, all pass); `api/start-attention.test.ts` (1). `api/api.test.ts` 45/45 and `start-commands` pass; `docs/nimblenewt/api-v1.md` regenerated.
- **Remains.** (1) Stale artifacts: no service says an artifact is stale (only the on-demand `verifyArtifact`, which reads every file); needs a definition and a cheap source. (2) The list does not yet carry the other overview kinds (blocked tasks, open waits, suspected stalls, failed events) although their data exists. (3) The `status.ask` overview is unchanged (no `taskId`/time-range filter there). (4) No index by agent or time: filters are applied while scanning, so a narrow filter on a big installation walks many tasks (bounded by `scanLimited`). (5) A started call that is still in flight is listed as `not finished`, like the `tools` view; there is no age threshold. (6) Other U13 items from slice 1 (tool activity and message-reference reads, long-running command states, restart-surviving subscription cursors).
- **Owner questions (provisional choices).** (a) What is a "stale artifact" (unverified for N days, files damaged, belongs to a task that changed after it was recorded)? None is listed until answered. (b) Should an in-flight tool call count as uncertain only after some age (provisional: always, as the `tools` view does)? (c) Operation name: `status.attention` was chosen over `status.overview` to keep the existing `status.ask` overview distinct. (d) `state` filters the task's state, not an item state; say if a per-kind state (for example gate observed state) is wanted. (e) Paused tasks whose owner is not an agent (a team or role owner) are listed with that owner's ID; the agent filter then matches agents only.

## U13 review fixes: attention cursors, unreachable workers, scan budget (2026-10-30)

- **Cursor leak (fixed, `attention` and `overview`).** A scan that ran out of budget used to hand back the ID of the last task it merely walked past (`<id>|9|` for attention, the bare ID for the overview), which could be another project's or an unreadable task. Such cursors are now sealed (AES-256-GCM, a per-`StatusService` random key, `~` plus base64url) and reveal nothing; an unsealable cursor is refused as `invalid_command`. Cursors naming a handed-out item (visible by construction) stay plain. Consequence: a sealed cursor is only valid on the service instance (process) that issued it, so one in flight across a controller restart is refused and the caller starts again.
- **Unreachable worker (changed, not reproducible as described).** The host check no longer depends on the execution state; it runs whenever the observation was reported by a `host:` principal. In this code `executionOf` can only say `working` or `unknown` for an active attempt (there is no silence/stall state), and `#execution` already turns `working` into `unknown` for a quiet or revoked host, so the old condition did not drop long-stale or revoked cases; the tests (long-stale report, then a revoked host) pass both before and after and stand as regression tests.
- **Per-task call-list budget (fixed).** The budget is now checked before every read of a task's calls (the first read of a visit always goes ahead so the cursor moves on) and each read asks for at most the remaining budget.
- **Tests.** `status/status.test.ts`: three suites "attention: ..." x 4 backends. The cursor and budget suites fail without the fix.

## T02b (part 1): in-flight policy on revocation

- A new run of a revoked version was already refused, and the start is checked inside the same transaction as the usage record. New: what a catalogue tool call that is already running does when its version is revoked. `ToolExecutionDeps.revocationPolicy` (read at the moment of revocation) answers `finish` (provisional default: the run ends on the bytes it started with) or `cancel` (the run's signal is aborted and the call ends as failed; a run that was registered but not yet started does not start). If the policy cannot be read, or answers anything else, the run is cancelled (a revocation is a safety act).
- `CatalogService.onRevoked(listener)` tells listeners after a revoke has committed (a replayed revoke tells again; listeners are idempotent; a throwing listener never undoes the revocation). `ToolExecutionService` subscribes and keeps the running calls by `name|version`.
- Tests (all four stores): policy finish / cancel / unreadable, a later call refused in each case.
- **Remains:** the composer does not yet pass `revocationPolicy` from a chat-settable policy key (the dependency is optional, so default is finish); `pause` as a third policy; cancellation of runs on other hosts (remote workers cannot run catalogue tools yet) and of runs in other processes (the listener is in-process; a restart already ends the run); retention of old and stale referenced versions (K06); promotion, state API and migration of paused tasks (as listed under T02 part 1).
- **Owner questions:** (1) Is `finish` the right default, or should a revocation cancel by default? (2) Which settings key should carry the policy, and should it differ per tool layer (system, shared, personal)?

### T02b review (2026-10-30): open items before wiring

- The revoke listener set lives on each `CatalogService` instance, and `start.ts` builds ad-hoc instances: when the revocation is wired, one shared instance (or a storage-level signal) must be used, or a revoke through another instance cancels nothing without failing. `ToolExecutionService` subscribes in its constructor and never unsubscribes: build it once.
- The test "replay" of a revoke uses a new command id; the same-command-id replay path (recorded result, listeners fire again) is untested. A runner's throwing abort listener would surface as an uncaught exception (the runner is internal).
- Nothing composes `revocationPolicy` or exposes `CatalogService.revoke` through the API or chat yet.
## H13f (part 3): choosing which event sources are watched

- `EventSourceSettingsService` (`events/source-settings.ts`), owner only. The setting is the list of sources turned off (`disabled`), so a source the host adds later is watched, as a controller with nothing set already does. API: `events.sources.get` (every configured source with type and `enabled`), `events.sources.set` (`disabled` replaces the list, optional `expectedRevision`), `events.sources.change` (`disable` / `enable`, leaves the rest alone; the form the chat uses so a request that waits does only what it says).
- Validation: IDs must look like source IDs; turning off must name a source this controller has (a typo turns nothing off silently); turning on may name an old entry so it can be cleared; at most 100; a source named in both lists is refused.
- `sourceLoops` reads the setting at every tick and polls only the sources left on. When the setting cannot be read nothing is polled that tick and the loop shows as failing (fail closed). A turned-off source is not polled from the next tick (one already in flight finishes).
- Chat op `events.sources.change`: always shown first (mode propose; provisional, because what is watched decides what wakes agents and spends work).
- Tests: `api/start-event-sources.test.ts` (rights, validation, stale revision, replay, chat proposal that survives a change made while it waits, all off, back on) and the fail-closed loop test.
- Remains in H13f: real repository, file, service-health, timer and model-availability sources need hosts to supply observations (the adapters exist in `events/adapters.ts`; nothing configures them); a chat view of the setting (the owner can read it through `events.sources.get`); a way for the host to add sources without a restart.
- Owner questions: (1) Should a source turned back on report what happened while it was off (provisional: yes, it resumes from its saved position; the alternative is to re-baseline it)? (2) Should chat apply a turn-off at once under the autonomous profile instead of always showing it first (provisional: always shown first)?

## H13f review fixes (event source setting)

- **Gap after a long off period.** `EventSource.retentionMs` is how far back a source can still see (the built-in `tasks` source: 7 days). When `SourceService` polls a source whose saved position (`at`) is older than that, it polls with no state (the source re-baselines), and returns `gap { from, to }`. `sourceLoops` tells the owner once per gap (stable id from source and `from`): "Events from <source> between T1 and T2 were not watched". This covers both re-enabling and a controller that was down. Turning a source off returns `warning` in the `events.sources.set/change` result for sources with a window.
- **Unreadable setting.** `sourceLoops` caches the last good off-list and uses it when the read fails (fail open on what the owner last said; failure logged through `onError`). With nothing cached it still polls nothing and fails the tick. After 5 consecutive failures the owner gets ONE notification per failure episode ("Event watching is not running: the source setting cannot be read.").
- **Critical sources (provisional, owner question).** `EventSource.critical?: boolean` (default false, `tasks` included): `EventSourceSettingsService` refuses to switch such a source off ("cannot be switched off; the controller relies on it"). Owner question open: which sources, if any, should be critical (candidates: tasks completion, since watches depend on it)?

### H13f: task completion is critical (owner, 2026-10-30)

The owner saw no reason to ignore built-in events. `tasks` (task completion) is now `critical: true`, so it cannot be switched off (watches and waiting agents depend on it). The off-list setting remains for noisy external sources that hosts add; a host marks any source `critical` if the controller relies on it.
## U11b remainder: the Notice level is never pushed

- `levelOf(item)` (exported from `notifications/`) gives the three levels from what an item is, not from a stored claim: safety stop, urgent or immediate is `urgent`; blocker, review request and owner question are `needs-you`; maintenance and presence are `notice`. `NotificationService.inbox` now returns each item with its `level`.
- A Notice is no longer listed in a digest or pushed. At a digest time `#collect` lists only the non-Notice items; the Notices waiting (up to 50 per pass) are marked `sent` with `countedAt` and counted in the same message as one line ("N notices in your inbox, no action needed."), a count only, never their text. When only Notices are waiting they are counted quietly: no digest record, no delivery, `runDue` returns no digest id. They stay in the inbox until the owner answers `ok`. Before, maintenance and presence items went out in the digest text like any other.
- Tests (`notifications.test.ts`, all three backends): levels told apart; external channel receives only the safety stop and one digest whose text has no Notice text; a Notice-only digest time sends nothing; `countedAt` set once; `ok` closes a Notice. The large-backlog test now uses 56 reviews (Notices no longer fill digests).
- Provisional (owner question): a digest time with only Notices sends nothing at all (the card says the stand-up report is the digest; that report does not read `level` yet).
- Remains in U11b: Notices do not expire (they still count against the 1000 open-item limit, so a flood of Notices can block new Needs-you items; they should be dropped after a retention time or exempted); the Notice count in the stand-up report and its opening with the Needs-you items; owner-marked critical tasks and goal-based critical path; the Urgent triggers for K01, H01/H09, A08, repeated denials, controller-down watchdog; escalation when the agent has nothing else to do and de-escalation by the dispatcher; the 09:00 digest only when no stand-up is scheduled; answering in place from the Needs-you view; deferred meeting items.

## U11b fixes (levels set by the controller)

- Emit takes a controller-only `level`; `levelOf` is an exhaustive kind map (maintenance and unnamed/missing level = needs-you; only presence is notice). All emit sites classified: budget request, incident to owner, stall concern, stall-detection-off, dispatcher-off, subscription expiry = needs-you; untold improvement = notice. `#escalateStale` covers every needs-you item.
- Notices are counted in a separate index list, exempt from the 1000 open-item limit, capped at 500 (oldest closed), and closed after `noticeRetentionDays` (default 7, `notifications.configure`). Quiet-counted Notices are carried into the next digest message (`mentionedAt`); the digest marks all Notices of the pass (changes chunked at 100 per command).
- Owner setting `levelByKind` (kind -> level, null = default) overrides the kind default; a safety stop stays urgent.

### No self-review, and review disabled for a one-agent project (owner decision, final)

- An agent never reviews its own work and there is no per-project override: the `allowSelfReview` option of `SubmissionService` is removed; `forbidden` on a review or qa report over one's own submission is unconditional (the sign-off self-check was already).
- `AgentService.reviewersAvailableIn(projectId, workerPrincipalId, now)` is the one helper: active agents with the `reviewer` role and a live effective grant in the project, never the worker. `SubmissionService` takes it as the `reviewersAvailableIn` port (wired in `startController`).
- A code submission now records `review: { required }`; when no other agent could review, `{ required: false, reason: "review_disabled_single_agent" }`. Nothing waits on a reviewer and no review request is created for it. The reason is on the submission record, so it is not silent. Adding a second reviewer-capable agent makes NEW submissions `required: true`; earlier records keep what they recorded.
- Not changed: tool/commit-gate reviews (`ReviewService`, `CommitGateService`) are owner/policy approvals of operations, not peer review of work, and still route as before. The landing check that reads `review.required` (integration policy `requiredChecks`) is not built yet; it must honor `review.required === false`.
- The earlier PROVISIONAL note on `allowSelfReview` (Q01b) is superseded by this entry.


## Stand-up report ordering by level (owner decision, 2026-10-30)

The owner's stand-up agenda opens with the Needs-you and Urgent inbox items (`needsOwnerFrom` now drops Notice-level items by the inbox `level`, which already applies the owner's `levelByKind`; Urgent first, then oldest), then the progress, and ends with one `noticeLine` ("N notices in your inbox, no action needed"). The count comes from the new `noticesFrom` / `StandupOptions.ownerNotices`, is read when the agenda is read (never stored in the prep record, so notice churn cannot rewrite it; `stable()` still compares only needs-you item ids), and is shown only where `needsOwner` is shown (owner, no task scope).
## M04f (part 3): the wake path for agents the host reports stopped

- `meetingWakeSink(host, { timeoutMs })` (`meetings/wake-sink.ts`) is the `WakeSink` the owner's `meeting.attend.wake` (`authorizeWake`, owner only, once per `<occurrence>:<agent>` key) now reaches. It checks the request is well formed (key equals `occurrence:agent`, an agent principal, a project), hands the host only those four fields, bounds the wait (default 30 s, 1 ms to 10 min, checked when the controller starts), and reports a failure as a fixed short message ("the host did not wake <agent>", plus "did not answer in time") so the host's own error text (paths, addresses) never reaches the owner. Nothing is retried or remembered: replay safety rests on the key; a host that answers late may still act, and a repeat is the same request.
- `StartOptions.meetingWake { recover(request), timeoutMs? }` is the host's hook, passed through `ComposeInput.meetingWake` to the attendance service. Absent (the default, so nothing changes for an installation that did not configure it): the owner's wake is refused with "no wake path", as before.
- Unchanged and still enforced by `authorizeWake`: only the owner may ask, the agent must be reported stopped or suspended right then, the room must be open, and the agent is `preparing` (not present) until the lifecycle reports it reachable; its other tasks stay held and it goes back to stopped when the meeting ends.
- Tests: `meetings/wake-sink.test.ts` (5: fields passed, malformed refused, host text hidden, timeout, bound), `api/start-meetings.test.ts` (composed controller: owner wake reaches the host once with the key, an available agent is refused and not sent, no host hook means refusal).
- Remains in M04f: nothing in the controller; a real host (L02/L03) must supply `recover` and make the stopped agent report available after it is up. Composing a real `safeLongRunning` (M04e) still waits on the owner question about what makes a long-running operation safe during a meeting.
- Owner questions: (1) Should the 30 s default wait for the host be chat-settable? (provisional: start-up option only). (2) Should the owner be told in chat when the host fails to wake the agent (provisional: the wake command returns the error; no separate notice).

## M04f fixes (wake failures, per-wake key, start-time check)

- A failed or slow host now reaches the owner as `unavailable` with the fixed text `the host did not wake <agent>[: it did not answer in time]`: the wake sink throws a `DomainError` (a plain `Error` was turned into the generic "the request could not be completed" by the state API). The host's own text is still dropped. Test goes through `meeting.attend.wake` with a failing, a hanging and an "Error('timed out')" host.
- The key sent to the host is now `<occurrence>:<agent>:<n>`; n counts the owner's wakes of that agent in that meeting (kept on the seat's `wake` record with the commandId that made it). An agent that crashes again mid-meeting and is woken again gets a new key, so the host no longer treats it as a repeat. A replay of the same wake command repeats the same key and does not count as a new wake. The sink validates the shape (`n` is 1 to 999999).
- `meetingWake.timeoutMs` is checked at the top of `startController` (`checkMeetingWakeTimeout`), so a bad value fails the start with a RangeError instead of switching the dispatcher off inside its try.
- The timeout uses a private sentinel; a host error whose message is "timed out" is no longer reported as a timeout.
- Tests: wake-sink (6), start-meetings (7: failing/hanging host, two wakes two keys plus replay, bad timeout, available agent refused with its exact message, replay of a wake command), attendance key updated. All fail against the old code.
## Q01c: listing submissions per task (2026-10-30)

- `SubmissionService.list(by, taskId, {kind?, afterId?, limit})` and API query `submission.list` (`taskId`, `kind?`, `limit?` 1-100 default 50, `after?`; result `{items, next?, scanLimited?}`). Visibility matches `get`: the owner sees every record of the task, an agent only the ones it made (reports redacted); a task the caller cannot read (no `task.read`, other task credential scope, non-agent non-owner) or that does not exist is `not_found`, so listing reveals nothing about other tasks. Work is bounded: at most 10 scan pages of 200 aggregates; `scanLimited` plus `next` when it stops early. Input (limit, kind, cursor) is validated. Docs regenerated.
- Tests: service (4 backends: owner vs agent visibility, other task excluded, paging, kind filter, hidden/unknown task, bad limit/kind/cursor) and through `startController` (owner, reviewer own-only, other project not_found, bad limit).
- Scan cost: the listing scans all submissions in ID order (no per-task index); fine until volumes grow, then add a task-keyed index.
- Remains of Q01: the states draft/submitted/under-review/accepted/rejected/superseded as versioned events and acceptance (tool completion alone cannot accept); review-state invalidation when the artifact changes; deliverable type/audience/access scope; operational-outcome deliverables; grouping source and exported artifacts; checking the task contract revision (S10); listing per project; task-credential test.
- Owner questions (provisional): should a reviewer/qa/director see the submission they are asked to review (today only the owner and the submitter see a record, so a reviewer cannot list the code it must review)? Is listing per project wanted, and for whom?

## Q01c fixes (submission list: cursor, visibility, reviewer read)

- HIGH fixed (information disclosure): `list` returned the last scanned row of the global submission table as `next`, and accepted any `sbm-` ID as `after`. `next` is now a sealed token (AES-256-GCM, per-instance random key, as the status scan cursors) holding caller ID, task ID and position; plain IDs, tampered, foreign-caller, other-task and other-instance cursors are `invalid_command`. A listing therefore never shows another task's or project's ID.
- A listing is not a feed (documented in the op description and `submission.list` docs): IDs are hash-ordered, so a new record can land before a held cursor; page to collect, do not poll for news.
- `get` now follows the same rule as `list`: an agent needs `task.read` in the submission's project and, with a task credential, that very task (before, `get` skipped both), plus having made the submission or being assigned to review it. Existing tests allowed the tightening.
- OWNER DECISION (final) implemented: a reviewer reads only the submission(s) its review request names, in `get` and `list`; no role-wide read. Service option `reviewAssignments(principalId, taskId) -> submission IDs`; the principal must still hold `reviewer` in the project. NOT WIRED in `startController`: there is no record yet linking a review request to a submission, so production has no assignments (reviewers see only their own) until the card that creates that record supplies the port.
- Scan limits are injectable (`listScan: {pageSize, reads}`, like `logScan`); tests cover `scanLimited` with a shrunk window and continuation by `next`, sealed/foreign/tampered cursors, report redaction in list, task-credential scope in list and get, get/list agreement, the reviewer read path.
- The comment on `KIND_ROLES` is reworded: a one-agent project holds several roles, but review is disabled (refused) rather than self-served unless `allowSelfReview` is set.
## H12k (part 3): the owner sets the limits for local agents; controller-owned default limits (2026-10-30)

- `defaultWorkspaceLimits(startup, setting)` (`api/worker-limits.ts`, pure): the owner's figures win per figure over `dispatch.local.limits`; nothing set gives `undefined` (nothing applied, as before). `WorkerLimitsSettingsService` (`api/worker-limits-settings.ts`) keeps the owner's figures (record `worker-limits-settings/main`), owner only, validated with the same bounds (`checkLocalWorkerLimits` now takes a label), `expectedRevision` for races, same command ID replays to the same revision.
- API: `workers.limits.get` (revision, owner's `limits`, `startup`, `effective`) and `workers.limits.set` (`limits` replaces the earlier setting; `{}` clears it). Chat: `workers.limits.set` is `propose` in every profile (provisional: resource decision, owner sees it first).
- Host builder: `build` services gain `currentLimits()`, read fresh per call (a change counts from the next agent launched; running agents keep theirs). It throws when the record cannot be read; the host must refuse the launch rather than run unlimited. `services.limits` (start-up figures) is unchanged.
- Test: `api/h12k-limits-setting.test.ts` (pure merge; through `startController`: owner only, seven bad shapes, required field, stale revision, replay, replace-not-merge, clear, builder sees each change). 542 tests pass over api, start-dispatch and chat; api docs regenerated.
- Not done (H12k stays planned): the host's `workspace` function does not yet call `currentLimits()` to fill `AttemptWorkspace.limits` (the checkout, git dir, home, scratch are still the operator's); no controller-owned default `workspace`; no per-role/task limits; the real-sandbox end-to-end test; MCP transport; `context`/`handoffFacts` default composition.
- Owner questions: (1) should limit changes be `propose` in chat in every profile (chosen) or follow the profile? (2) should a change also apply to running agents (needs a restart of them; not done)? (3) should the owner's figures be allowed to exceed start-up ones, or is start-up a ceiling (chosen: no ceiling)?

## H12k review fixes: limits are read per launch, chat merges instead of replacing

- No composed workspace builder exists in the repo: `dispatch.local.build` is supplied by the host, and `AttemptWorkspace.limits` is filled by that host code (the controller only passes `build` its services). So the controller cannot itself refuse a launch; the contract is made explicit in types instead. `build`'s services no longer carry the static start-up `limits` (removed, not made a getter), so a host cannot read stale figures; the only way to get limits is the required `currentLimits()`, which reads the owner's setting over the start-up figures at each call. A host that still reads `services.limits` no longer compiles, and one that ignores `currentLimits` has no figures to apply. `currentLimits()` throws when the setting is unreadable (damaged record, storage fault); the host must let that fail the launch visibly and never start the agent unlimited. The enforcement itself therefore remains the host's duty and is not checked by anything in this repo beyond the test host in `h12k-limits-enforce.test.ts`.
- New operation `workers.limits.change` (`set`, `unset` list, optional `expectedRevision`): merges into the current setting like `events.sources.change`. Chat now proposes `workers.limits.change` (the chat entry for `workers.limits.set` is removed); `workers.limits.set` stays for the API. A proposal made at revision 1 and accepted after an API change keeps the API change.
- Tests (`api/h12k-limits-enforce.test.ts`): launch refused when the setting is unreadable and figures seen after a change; effective()/get() throw on damaged records and storage faults (fail-closed coverage; this behaviour already held and the test pins it); replay of a command ID with different limits is `command_conflict`, with the same limits it replays.
- The doc comment for `eventSourcesOff` in `dispatch-compose.ts` is back above it.

## Supervisor escalation ladder (owner decision 2026-10-30, follow-up of V02b)

- Decision: a stuck agent's stall concern goes to its supervisor first, then up the supervisor chain, finally to the owner. Time per level is chat-settable, default 24 hours. This replaces V02b's single 30-minute jump to the owner (`StallOptions.escalateAfterMs` default is now 24 h and is the installation profile value for levels the owner's setting does not name).
- Setting: `EscalationLadderService` (`health/escalation-ladder.ts`, record `escalation-ladder-settings/main`): owner only, `hours` = whole hours for level 0, 1, 2 ... (1..720, at most 16 levels; a level past the list waits the default), replaces the list, `[]` clears, optional `expectedRevision`, command id scoped to the owner. API `escalation.ladder.get` / `escalation.ladder.set`; chat `escalation.ladder.set` (`propose`). The pass reads the hours each tick; an unreadable or damaged record stops the pass (no climb at a time nobody set).
- Concern record gains `escalatedTo` (`agent:<ID>` or `owner`), `escalationLevel` and `escalationTrail` (last 20 climbs: level, to, at, skipped supervisors with reasons, at most 10 each). `escalatedAt` is the time of the last climb; level n waits from `escalatedAt` (level 0 from `lastChangedAt`). One climb per concern per pass; each write is keyed by concern and revision, so a repeated pass or a restart repeats no step. A climb clears `notifiedAt` so the new holder is told once.
- Who is next: walk up `supervisorId` from the current holder. Passed over, with the reason recorded: retired agent, no active identity, the task's own owner, and an agent that holds none of `task.read`, `assignment.read`, `assignment.manage` for the task (effective rights, restrictions included: "cannot see the task"). A repeat in the chain, a missing agent record, or a chain deeper than `AGENT_LIMITS.chain` ends at the owner with the reason. No supervisor left: `owner`, the top; nothing climbs further.
- Access: the agent the concern is escalated to can read and decide that one concern while it still holds a right to see the task (checked at each read). The routed supervisor keeps its access; the next holder replaces the earlier escalated one. The task's own owner still cannot decide its own concern.
- Notices: an agent target gets a controller notice on the task (`stall-esc-<hash(concern|escalatedAt|level)>`, stable across retries); if it can no longer be told (`forbidden`), the owner gets a needs-you item naming it. The owner at the top gets the needs-you item as before.
- Tests: `health/stall.test.ts` (climb order with the owner's hours and the installation default, skipped supervisor with reason, restart repeats nothing, access of holder and skipped agents, default 24 h, unreadable setting, forced loop ends at the owner), `api/v02d-ladder-setting.test.ts` (owner only, bounds, replay, stale revision, clear).
- Remains: the standing recovery action ladder after the owner (V02c); a per-project override of the hours; an owner-set pause of the ladder; the earlier escalated holders lose sight of the concern when it climbs (kept simple).
- Owner questions: (1) should an earlier holder keep read access after the concern climbs? (2) should `escalation.ladder.set` be `apply` in chat rather than `propose`?

### Supervisor escalation ladder: review fixes

- Who may decide a concern once it has climbed (the rule, also in the doc comment of `escalateUndecided`): the owner; holders of `assignment.manage` in the project; the supervisor it was first routed to; and the one current holder (`escalatedTo`) only while it can still see the task. Supervisors it climbed past, and earlier holders, no longer see it. The task's own owner never decides on its own concern.
- Concerns escalated by the first version of V02b (`escalatedAt` set, no `escalatedTo`) are read as held by the owner (`readConcern`, applied on every read), so they are not climbed to a supervisor and told again. The notice id is unchanged, so it is not repeated.
- An unreadable or damaged ladder setting no longer throws out of `escalateUndecided`: nothing climbs, the notices already owed are still returned and told, and the owner gets one needs-you item per episode (`ladderDamaged` option, id `stall-ladder-damaged-<hash of the episode start>`; the episode ends when the setting reads again). The episode is held in memory, so a controller restart during the same damage tells the owner once more.
- Concerns that have nothing left to climb (routed to the owner, or parked with it) and no notice owed are left out before the `limit` of 100, so they cannot crowd out others.
- A change of route (the agent's supervisor changed or retired, so the route moved) starts the ladder again: `escalatedAt`, `notifiedAt`, `escalatedTo`, `escalationLevel` and `escalationTrail` are dropped and the new route's clock starts at the change.
- A holder that cannot be told (`forbidden` on the notice) is no longer left holding the concern: `StallService.holdWithOwner` parks it with the owner (`escalatedTo: "owner"`, level and time kept so the owner's notice has the id the supervisor's would have had), and the owner is told. It does not climb back down. The dispatch-compose wiring of this has no test of its own (the service method is tested).
- The skipped-supervisor reasons in `escalationTrail` are shown only to the owner and the current holder; every other reader (the stalled agent's supervisor, managers) gets the trail without `skipped`.
- `#nextHolder`: the walk's `seen` set is the holders visited (current holder, routed supervisor, earlier trail), no longer pre-loaded with the task owner, so meeting the task's owner is passed over with "is the task's own owner" and the walk goes on instead of stopping with a "loops back" reason.
- Tests: legacy-escalated concern, damaged setting (owed notice returned, one notice per episode, new episode after mending), limit starvation, route change mid-climb (new supervisor, then owner route), trail redaction and `holdWithOwner`, task owner in the chain; the retired-chain test now actually retires an agent.
## K06b first slice: storage delete primitive and incident purge (2026-10-30)

- **Storage:** a fourth `Change`, `{ type: "delete", ref, expectedRevision }`, inside `applyOperation` (memory, SQLite, PostgreSQL; conformance, plus the parity workload now draws deletes). It inherits the operation's epoch fence, idempotency (a repeat is answered from the stored result and removes nothing more; the same ID with other content is `idempotency_conflict`), all-or-nothing commit and the revision guard (`revision_conflict`/`not_found`, nothing removed). The result lists the removed revision. Validation refuses (as `invalid_input`, identically on every backend) a removal with no audit entry whose `subject` is that aggregate, a message announcing the removed aggregate, and the same ref twice in one operation. Work is bounded by the existing per-operation limits.
- **Known:** a later `create` of the same ref restarts at revision 1 (no tombstone), so a stale holder of revision 1 could pass a guard on a re-created record; callers that expire a kind must not reuse its IDs (incident IDs are derived hashes of a counter generation, so they are not reused). Deliveries, timers and effects naming a removed aggregate are untouched. Snapshots/backups simply no longer contain the row.
- **Domain:** `IncidentService.purge(by, { olderThanDays (30..3650, REQUIRED, no default), limit = 200 (1..1000), projectId? })`, owner or service only: removes resolved, archived (K06 soft archive) incidents archived longer ago than the window and not escalated-but-untold, each by guarded delete with the revision just read, with an `responsibility.incident.purge` audit record per removal (project, signature, archivedAt). Returns the count removed.
- **Remains for K06b:** the tier policy itself (chat-settable per-kind ages, unset falls back to the profile, owner-only, recorded, confirmed back with old/new value); the "shows what it will remove before it runs" dry-run and the preview-then-confirm flow; wiring `archiveLoops`/a purge loop in `start.ts`; archive-then-restore of the original; derived copies (summaries, indexes) following the source; protection of anything a resumable task or replay references (needs a reference check per kind); other kinds (logs, scratch, transcripts, thinking at 14 days: needs adapter support); an index so the scan need not read every record; a tombstone if ID reuse ever matters.

### K06b review fixes

- `IncidentService.purge` now also swallows `not_found` (the record was removed between its read and its write by someone else) and carries on with the rest; it was only `stale_revision` before, so a lost race aborted the whole purge. Tested with a storage wrapper that removes the record just before the service's own removal.
- Tombstone (replaces the "Known" item above, which said a re-created ref restarts at revision 1): each removal also writes an aggregate of the reserved kind `tombstone` (id `t-<sha256 of kind/id>`, body `{ kind, id, revision }` = the removed revision), in the same transaction, on memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL (`storage/tombstone.ts`). A later `create` of the same ref starts at tombstone revision + 1 (chosen over refusing the create, because incident IDs and other derived IDs may legitimately be created again, and revision continuity already makes a stale holder fail its guard with `revision_conflict`). The tombstone is an ordinary row of the `aggregates` table, so snapshots, backups and restores carry it with no format change; operations naming the kind are refused as `invalid_input`. It stays for the life of the store (one small row per removal; a second removal of the same ref updates it). PostgreSQL takes a transaction advisory lock on the ref in both create and delete so a create racing a removal reads the committed tombstone.
- Tests: conformance (all backends; create, update, remove, re-create continues at 3, stale holders refused, second removal, reserved kind), a removal racing an update and a create of the same ref (six rounds, one consistent outcome), snapshot/restore carries the tombstone and the restored store continues the revision.
- Dangling references: notifications (and other records) that name a purged incident by ref are not cleaned up; a reader following such a ref gets `not_found`. Purge only touches resolved, archived incidents whose escalation was told, so nothing the owner still has to act on points at one, but old inbox items may. Left for the tier policy of K06b (a reference check per kind is already listed under Remains).
## Reassignment by decision applies at once, with a warning (owner decision 2026-10-30)

- The meeting `task.reassign` applier (`taskReassignApplier`) no longer refuses a new holder that lacks `attempt.work` or `task.read`; there is no accept-first step. It moves the task through the assignment service, then computes the missing rights with the same effective-grant checks (`missingRights`, wired in `api/start.ts`) and calls a warn hook.
- `reassignWarningSink` (`meetings/reassign-warning.ts`) files one controller-set needs-you notification for the owner and a best-effort notice to the meeting's chair, naming the agent and the missing rights. Command IDs derive from the change's own (`mtg:<decision>:<change>`), so a replay records nothing new; a replay that finds the move done re-calls the hook to cover a crash between move and warning.
- Not changed: the hand-off service (`lifecycle/handoff-sources.ts` `ineligible`) still refuses a recipient with no right to work in the project; a follow-up card should decide whether hand-offs also move with a warning.
- Review fixes. (1) The dispatcher's grant step (`#missingGrants`) now always requires `attempt.work` and `task.read` on the task for the assignee, besides the contract's tools; an agent without them (for example one a meeting handed the task to) is not admitted: the normal `grant_needed` blocker names the missing rights, and the next tick after the owner grants them starts the attempt. So no task credential or work order is issued without the rights, while the reassignment itself still applies at once and warns the owner. (2) The owner warning is no longer swallowed: a failure to record it propagates (a refusal from the notification service becomes `unavailable`), the change stays "applying" and the replay warns again; only the chair's notice is best effort (in `reassignWarningSink`). (3) Tests rewritten: the replay is driven through the real branch (warning write fails once, then succeeds on replay: one inbox item) and the unit test asserts the warning count. (4) The replay warns only when the generation after the observed one was made by this decision: the reassignment's reason now carries the change's command ID and `history()` is consulted, so a later hand move of the owner to the same agent warns nothing. (5) The "is an active agent" check now runs after the "already done" check, so a replay of a completed move succeeds for a holder that has since been disabled. The doc comment that called the move "not a widening of rights" is replaced.


- **No ceiling on agreed raises or grants by default (owner decision 2026-10-30).** The provisional per-raise caps (5e9 millionths, 4 h compute) and the 30-day limit on an agreed grant are gone as fixed rules. They are now optional owner settings (`agreed-limits-settings/main`: `raiseMaxCostMicros`, `raiseMaxComputeMs`, `grantMaxDays`), unset = unlimited, changed with `agreed.limits.change` (`set`/`unset`, optional `expectedRevision`, owner only; chat mode propose) and read with `agreed.limits.get` (owner only). `BudgetService.raiseAgreed` (policy-agreed raises only) and `GrantService.grantAgreed` read the setting fresh at each carry-out; an unreadable or damaged setting refuses the carry-out rather than meaning "no ceiling". Unchanged: rights re-check at carry-out, rights_withdrawn refusal, only-what-was-agreed amounts, grant must be future and a valid time. The owner-initiated standing-grant limit (365 days, chat/policy-edit.ts) is a different rule and was left alone.
- Review fixes. (1) `BudgetService.raiseAgreed` now checks the policy ceiling inside the command (in `build`, after the runner has looked for a record of this command ID), like `GrantService.grantAgreed` checks "already made" first: a raise committed before a crash is answered as made on replay even if the owner has since lowered `raiseMaxCostMicros`; a new raise is still held to the ceiling. (2) `AgreedLimitsSettingsService.effective()` throws a `DomainError` (`invalid_command`, field `limits`) for a damaged record instead of a plain `Error`: the meeting applier only turns DomainErrors into a failed change, so the change now fails visibly (and the owner is told by the existing failed-change path) instead of staying "applying" and being retried without a word. A storage fault while reading is still the storage's own error and is retried. (Deviation from the review text: `unavailable` is what the applier rethrows and retries, so it would not have made the change fail.) (3) Removed the orphaned doc comment on a deleted constant in `security/grants.ts`.
- With no `grantMaxDays` set, an agreed grant may carry a far-future expiry (effectively permanent); that is the owner's decision of 2026-10-30, and the owner can set `grantMaxDays` to bound it.


### Resume retry limit as an owner setting (owner decision 2026-10-30)

- The blocked-round retry limit of a resume check (`maxRounds`, 1..10, default 3) is now an owner-only setting: `resume.settings.get` / `resume.settings.set` (`maxRounds` or null to clear, `expectedRevision`, replay-safe by command ID), proposed first in chat (`resume.settings.set`, mode propose). Stored in `ResumeSettingsService` (`resume-settings` aggregate).
- `ResumeCheckService.withEpoch` takes an optional `rounds()` provider, read once inside `start` for a new check and written into the check's record; a running check keeps the figure it started with (retryable/exhausted/churn all read the record). A damaged stored value throws and refuses the start rather than using a wrong limit. The static `maxRounds` option remains for tests and as the fallback when no provider is given. Wired in `api/start.ts`; unset means the installation default (3).
- Review fix: a damaged stored retry limit no longer blocks resumes (before, every resume start threw inside `build`, so every resumed attempt was skipped silently). `ResumeSettingsService.effective()` now falls back to the installation default (3) and calls an optional `warn` once per damage episode; `api/start.ts` wires it to one controller-set `maintenance` / `needs-you` notification whose command ID is `resume-settings-damaged:<record revision>` (stable per episode; the owner's next `resume.settings.set` repairs it and a new damage is a new revision). A failure to send the warning does not stop the resume; the next read tries again. A fixed `maxRounds` option is no longer validated when `rounds()` is supplied (it was ignored). Tests: `continuation/resume-settings.test.ts`, `api/resume-settings-api.test.ts`.
## First-run guide and setup readiness (owner question 2026-10-30; card U14, planned)

- The owner asked how a person does the initial configuration before the first agent exists. Finding: there is no launcher, installer or first-run step; `startController` is a library function, the state API is in-process only (the HTTP listener carries conversations), nothing loads the configuration document into the start, the routing table, host and agent credentials and the approval profile are changed from code or chat only, and the local worker host is not composed (H12k). `docs/nimblenewt/getting-started.md` is the step-by-step guide that works today (a tested start script plus state-API calls) and marks each gap with its card.
- Added card U14 (first-run setup assistant) and put it in D05's dependencies. The card count is 309.
- Built the read-only owner operation `setup.readiness` (`setup/readiness.ts`, `SetupReadinessService`): per item (owner, approval profile, project, model route, host, notifications, agent, first task) a state of done, default, missing or optional, what was found, whether it is required and how to set it; `ready` when every required item is done and `next` names the first required one missing. It reads records only (a count is the most it says about a project or agent), is refused to non-owners and task credentials, and changes nothing. A host counts only after it has announced itself. Test: `api/start-setup.test.ts`.
- Facts the guide records that were found by running it: the routing table is refused unless the coordinator and safety-supervisor roles each have a profile with two entries on different endpoints; the start refuses an unsupported file system (for example tmpfs) unless `--allow-unsupported-environment` is given; `integration.set` names its project argument `project`.
## Optional grant lengths, clearable model limits, escalation off (nn-sa-optgrants)

Owner rule: limits are optional and every setting can be changed and switched off by chat.

- Chat standing grants: `lengthDays: null` means a grant with no end (the owner's words must say so: permanent, no end, never expires, indefinitely, forever...; otherwise `unsupported_value`). It is still a proposal; the preview says "permanent: it has no end time" or, for a length, the real end time if applied now. The grant is made without `expiresAt` (security/grants.ts is unchanged; AGREED_GRANT_MAX_MS belongs to meeting grants, not these).
- The fixed 365-day ceiling is gone. Two optional installation settings replace it: `grants.maxDays` (unset = no maximum; while set, a grant with no end or a longer one is refused, offered lengths are cut to it, and it is checked again when the edit is applied) and `grants.defaultDays` (unset = 30 days, never above the maximum). Both are changed and removed through the existing chat `setting` edit (shown first). A retry of an edit already applying keeps its stored length, so a maximum set meanwhile cannot strand it half done.
- A spending grant may say "no limit": `spendLimit: null` (words must say no limit/unlimited) is stored as the term `spendUnlimited: true` (excludes `spendLimit`); the engine accepts it for a spend grant. Without any statement a spending grant is still refused (`needs_limit`).
- `grant.create` chat preview printed "permanent" always; it now prints the real `expiresAt` when given (chat/commands.ts describe).
- `model-budget.set` (routing/fallback.ts): a field given as null removes that limit, others stay (chat: "remove the limit"; always shown first because it is a raise).
- `notifications.configure`: `escalateAfterHours: null` turns escalation off; a number turns it on again.
- Why no more: no typed per-field "enable/disable" flag beyond null/unset; each limit is simply absent when off.

### Optional grant length: review fixes
- A large finite `lengthDays` can no longer stand in for "no end": a number must appear in the owner's own words (`lengthInWords`), else the edit is refused as `unsupported_value` like the spend limit; and there is a hard ceiling of 36500 days (`GRANT_DAYS_CEILING`, about 100 years) on a length, an `until` date and a length picked at apply time. The end-time arithmetic is also caught: a `RangeError` becomes a `Refusal` (`invalid_length`), never a crash.
- The "no end" and "no limit" owner words (`NO_END_WORDS`, `NO_LIMIT_WORDS`) are read per sentence with negation (`saysWords`): a negation, question or musing in the rest of the sentence rules the match out ("don't make it permanent", "not unlimited"), and "taking forever" is a complaint, not an order. The words that are themselves negations ("no end", "doesn't expire") are removed before the negation check.
- `#run` for a grant fails closed: when the decision has neither `expiresAt` nor `permanent: true` it refuses (`invalid_transition`) instead of making a grant with no end.
- `grants.maxDays` scope: it binds chat policy edits (the owner's setting is read on prepare and again on apply) and now the standing-rule proposal path too: `ApprovalLoadService.accept` takes an optional `maxDays` reader; a length the owner picked or stated beyond it is refused, the usual default is cut to it and says so. Provisional: the reader is an option only; no production code constructs `ApprovalLoadService` yet, so wire it to `configuration.effective` when it is composed.
- `describe("grant.create", ...)` now puts the end ("ends ..." or "permanent: no end time") before the long basis and terms, so line truncation cannot drop it.
- Merge note: rebased onto main; both sides of the notes conflict kept.

### Optional grant length, second review round (provisional choices)

- Owner wording is normalized (curly quotes become straight) before the negation, no-end and no-limit checks. A negation now refuses only when it directly governs the matched words: up to six words before them in the same clause (clauses end at a comma, "but" or "and"). "Not permanent", "don't make it permanent" and "never permanent" are still refused; "permanent instead of a week" and "permanent, I don't want to keep approving this" are accepted. Doubt still fails closed (no end is never assumed). "never expires" and "doesn't expire" count as no-end words.
- `lengthInWords` accepts digits and number words (one to twelve, twenty, thirty) for days, weeks, fortnights, months and years; a month is 28 to 31 days and a year 365 or 366 (tolerance, not equality).
- The `grants.maxDays` reader for `ApprovalLoadService` stays unwired: nothing constructs `ApprovalLoadService` yet. Wire it when that service is constructed.
## Dispatcher limits optional (owner rule: time and money limits are optional, off by default, changeable and enable/disable-able through chat)

- The attempt time cap (was 4 h) and the dispatcher's attempt count (was 3) are now OFF by default. `DISPATCH_LIMITS` no longer has `attemptMs` / `maxAttempts`; `AttemptDispatcherOptions.attemptMs` / `maxAttempts` stay as optional start-up figures (absent = no limit). A dispatch record's `expiresAt` (and `WorkOrder.expiresAt`, the remote placement's `expiresAt`, the accept reply) is therefore optional: absent means the attempt has no time limit. The worker lease still has to be kept (a worker that stops beating is lost as before), the credential still ends with the attempt, and the claim/expiry checks treat an absent expiry as "never".
- New owner-only setting `dispatch.limits.get` / `dispatch.limits.change` (`api/dispatch-limits-settings.ts`): `attemptMinutes` (1 to 525600) and `maxAttempts` (1 to 1000), each on/off. `set` turns on with a figure (null turns off), `disable` turns off but keeps the figure, `enable` turns on again with the kept figure, `unset` forgets the entry so the start-up option (or no limit) applies; a limit is named once; `expectedRevision` optional; merge-style so a chat proposal accepted late keeps changes made meanwhile. Chat proposes `dispatch.limits.change` (CHAT_OPS). Replay of a command ID returns the first result. The dispatcher reads the setting on every claim and every re-admission (`options.limits`), so a change counts from the next claim; an attempt already running keeps the expiry it was given. If the record is unreadable the claim / re-admission throws and nothing starts (fail closed).
